#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe the cli that turns dash into a dot
# @meta require-tools git
set -euo pipefail

DASH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)"
# joins the items of a list value; `get` prints one item per line
SEP=$'\x1f'

# layers in fold order, later wins: base, global, local
_layer_file() {
    case "$1" in
    base) echo "$DASH_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "${SKOGAI_GLOBAL_CONFIG:-$HOME/.skogai/config}" ;;
    local)
        local root
        root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
        echo "${SKOGAI_LOCAL_CONFIG:-$root/.skogai/config}"
        ;;
    esac
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
        echo "$f"
        _local_md "$f"
    done
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under --scope if given, with `_` read as `-`. a list is one
# value, its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${argc_scope:-}" yq --front-matter=extract '
        select(document_index == 0) | select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")' "$1"
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag
    for layer in base global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    local fm
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$file")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="file:$file"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# the frontmatter path of a key in a --file layer: the key minus --scope
_file_key() {
    local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
    if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
        [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || { echo "key $key is outside --scope $scope" >&2; return 2; }
        key="${key#"$scope".}"
    fi
    [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad key: $1" >&2; return 2; }
    echo "$key"
}

# @cmd read and write key/value config across base, global and local layers
config() { :; }

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key!
config::get() {
    local env line resolved key="${argc_key,,}"
    key="${key//_/-}"
    env="$(_env_name "$key")"
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    line="$(awk -F'\t' -v k="$key" '$1 == k' <<<"$resolved")"
    if [[ -z $line && -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
        line="$key"$'\t'"${!env}"$'\t'"env:$env"
    fi
    [[ -n $line ]] || exit 1
    if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
    else
        cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
    fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key!
# @arg value!
config::set() {
    local file key
    if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"
        K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
    git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key!
config::unset() {
    local file key
    if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
        K="$key" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::list() {
    local key value origin item resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
            if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
                printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
            else
                printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
            fi
        done <<<"$value$SEP"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::env() {
    local key value origin resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
config::files() {
    local layer file
    for layer in base global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$layer" "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
    done
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' file "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
    done < <(_file_layers)
}

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

## Changes, in order

1. **Fix `skogai` on `PATH`:** done 2026-10-16. The broken uv `skogai-cli` is uninstalled and `~/.local/bin/skogai` links to `~/skogai/dash-skogai/bin/skogai`.
2. **dash `bin/skogai`:** done in `~/skogai` commit `9ad0067`. It adds `--file` (repeatable) and `--scope` to `get`/`list`/`env`/`files`, plus `set`/`unset --file`, which write `x.local.md`. Lists print one item per line, `~` removes a key, and an unreadable layer exits `2`. `get` reads `_` as `-`. Still open: `set --file` writes the key as typed, so `b_c` and `b-c` can both end up in one file.
3. **skogai-core `git-steps.sh`:** done. It reads `skogai config list` from the git root and falls back to env (`SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP`, ...) when no working `skogai` is on PATH, with the names dash's rule gives (`.` → `_`, `-` dropped, since dash `820af35`).
4. **skogai-core `settings.sh` and `register.ts`:** done. Both read `skogai config list --file <root>/.claude/skogai-core.md --scope skogai-core` and fall back to reading the `.local.md` themselves when `skogai` doesn't know `--file`, for a `skogai` without `--file` (another machine, or none installed). Keys are kebab-case (`log-path`); `_` still reads.
5. **mise:** the `SKOGAI_*_ON_*` lines in `~/.config/mise/config.toml` are commented out and use the old names. Put the values in `~/.skogai/config` instead, and drop the lines.
6. **Delete** the copies of `validate-settings.sh` / `example.local.md` in `dash-skogai/`, once the dash type checks config.

## Decisions for skogix

- **Format split.** This doc proposes git-config for layers 1–3, frontmatter for files. The alternative is frontmatter everywhere (`.skogai/config.md`), which makes dash's existing CLI and spec change.
- **Global layer.** `~/.skogai/config`, as dash says, or `/skogai` per decision 0005, or `$XDG_SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR`? Today `~/.skogai` is nearly empty and the XDG vars are set but used by nothing.
- **Where the XDG vars come from.** They're in the systemd user environment with no known source file. No session sets `SKOGAI_*_ON_*` any more: the mise lines are commented out.
- **Strict keys** (dash TODO "strict keys declared by types, or free-form?"). A type could declare a plugin's keys, types and defaults, and its defaults would be the base layer for that scope.
- **Env names for scoped keys.** `skogai-core.log-path` → `SKOGAI_SKOGAICORE_LOGPATH`. Dropping `-` means `on-stop` and `onstop` share one env name.

## Left out on purpose

- A project layer distinct from local.

**Why it's easy to move**
- The script has one tie to dash: `DASH_DIR` → `$DASH_DIR/config`, the base layer. The rest is git config, yq and argc.
- Those base keys (`stage.*`, `commit.*`, `merge.*`, `event.log-path`) are settings for skogai-core, read by `git-steps.sh` and the event log. So the plugin's defaults currently live in another repo.
- skogai-core is the only thing that calls it (`git-steps.sh`, `settings.sh`, `register.ts`). Its `CONFIG.md` already documents the design, and it already falls back to env or reading `.local.md` directly when `skogai` isn't on PATH.

**What would need to change**
- Move `bin/skogai` and `config` into `plugins/skogai-core/`. `DASH_DIR` then resolves to the plugin root without any other edits.
- Point `~/.local/bin/skogai` at the marketplace source (`~/.local/src/marketplace/plugins/skogai-core/bin/skogai`), not the plugin cache. The cache path includes the version number (`skogai-core/0.8.0`), so a link there breaks on every bump.
- Update the paths in dash's `type/config.md`, `type/tool/skogai.md`, `workflows/skogai.md` and `README.md`, and in skogai-core's `CONFIG.md`. Those are only path references.

**One thing to decide first**
- The script describes itself as "the cli that turns dash into a dot", and `config` is meant as a general SkogAI setting, not something specific to Claude Code. If you want config usable from mise or a plain shell without a Claude plugin installed, keep the spec (`type/config.md`) in dash and treat skogai-core as the place the CLI ships from.
- If `skogai` will eventually grow beyond `config`, **skogai-runner** (also argc) would be the better home, since it's the generic one.

My recommendation: move the CLI and the base `config` to skogai-core, and keep the type spec in dash. Want me to do it?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe the cli that turns dash into a dot
# @meta require-tools git
set -euo pipefail

DASH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)"
# joins the items of a list value; `get` prints one item per line
SEP=$'\x1f'

# layers in fold order, later wins: base, global, local
_layer_file() {
    case "$1" in
    base) echo "$DASH_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "${SKOGAI_GLOBAL_CONFIG:-$HOME/.skogai/config}" ;;
    local)
        local root
        root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
        echo "${SKOGAI_LOCAL_CONFIG:-$root/.skogai/config}"
        ;;
    esac
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
        echo "$f"
        _local_md "$f"
    done
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under --scope if given, with `_` read as `-`. a list is one
# value, its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${argc_scope:-}" yq --front-matter=extract '
        select(document_index == 0) | select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")' "$1"
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag
    for layer in base global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    local fm
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$file")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="file:$file"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# the frontmatter path of a key in a --file layer: the key minus --scope
_file_key() {
    local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
    if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
        [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || { echo "key $key is outside --scope $scope" >&2; return 2; }
        key="${key#"$scope".}"
    fi
    [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad key: $1" >&2; return 2; }
    echo "$key"
}

# @cmd read and write key/value config across base, global and local layers
config() { :; }

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key!
config::get() {
    local env line resolved key="${argc_key,,}"
    key="${key//_/-}"
    env="$(_env_name "$key")"
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    line="$(awk -F'\t' -v k="$key" '$1 == k' <<<"$resolved")"
    if [[ -z $line && -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
        line="$key"$'\t'"${!env}"$'\t'"env:$env"
    fi
    [[ -n $line ]] || exit 1
    if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
    else
        cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
    fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key!
# @arg value!
config::set() {
    local file key
    if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"
        K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
    git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key!
config::unset() {
    local file key
    if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
        key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
        file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
        K="$key" \
            yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
        return
    fi
    file="$(_target_file)"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::list() {
    local key value origin item resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
            if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
                printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
            else
                printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
            fi
        done <<<"$value$SEP"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
config::env() {
    local key value origin resolved
    resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
    [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
        printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
    done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
config::files() {
    local layer file
    for layer in base global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$layer" "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
    done
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' file "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
    done < <(_file_layers)
}

# Complete Patterns

## File/path/directory

1. Use argc semantic

```sh
# @option --output <file>
# @option --cwd <dir>
# @option --file
# @arg path...
```

Automatically determine based on `<file>`, `<dir>`, `--file`, `path`, etc.

2. Use `_argc_util_comp_path`

```sh
_choice_fn() {
    _argc_util_comp_path
}
```

## Multiple values

```sh
_choice_fn() {
  printf "%s\n" abc def ijk
}
```

```sh
_choice_fn() {
  cat <<-'EOF'
abc
def
ijk
EOF
}
```

```sh
_choice_fn() {
  echo -e "value\tdescribe value"
  echo -e "other value\tdescribe other value"
  echo -e "another value\tdescribe another value"
}
```

```sh
_choice_fn() {
  cat <<-'EOF'
value	describe value"
other value	describe other value"
another value	describe another value"
EOF
}
```

## Key value pairs, keys are constants

```sh
_choice_option() {
    cat <<-'EOF' | _argc_util_comp_kv =
AddKeysToAgent=yes,ask,confirm,no
AddressFamily=any,inet,inet6
CertificateFile=__argc_value=file
HostKeyAlgorithms=`_choice_hostkeyalgorithms`
EOF
}
```

```
$ scp -o <tab>
AddKeysToAgent=   AddressFamily=    CertificateFile=    HostKeyAlgorithms=

$ scp -o AddKeysToAgent=
yes   ask   confirm   no
```

## Key value pairs, keys are dynamic

```sh
_choice_user_group() {
    _argc_util_mode_kv ':'
    if [[ -z "$argc__kv_prefix" ]]; then
        _module_os_user | _argc_util_transform suffix=: nospace
    else
        _module_os_group
    fi
}
```

```
$ scp <tab>
user1:    user2:    user3:

$ scp user1:<tab>
group1    group2    group3
```

## Tag value pairs

The preceding position argument determines how to complete the following position argument.

```sh
_choice_address_add() {
    cat <<-'EOF' | _argc_util_comp_tv
dev=`_choice_ip_device`;;the name of the device to add the address to.
local=;;the address of the interface.
peer=;;the address of the remote endpoint for pointopoint interfaces.
broadcast=;;the broadcast address on the interface.
label=;;Each address may be tagged with a label string.
scope=`_choice_ip_scope`;;the scope of the area where this address is valid.
EOF
}
```

```
$ ip address add 33.33.33.33 dev <tab>
lo      wlp0s20f3     enp0s31f6  

$ ip address add 33.33.33.33 scope <tab>
0 (global)     255 (nowhere)  200 (site) 
```

## Multiple parts

Complete values that are divided into sections by level, such as paths.

```sh
_choice_unstaged_file() {
    _git status --porcelain | gawk '{
    if (substr($0, 2, 1) != " ") {
        print substr($0, 4)
    }
}' | _argc_util_comp_parts /
}
```

```
$ git add completions/<tab>
cargo   git.sh    go.sh   
```

If you don't set multi parts. The completions will be

```
$ git add completions/<tab>
completions/cargo/audit.sh
completions/cargo/binstall.sh
completions/git.sh
completions/go.sh
```

## Multiple values

Multiple values are separated by `,` `|` and so on.

### Use argc modifier
```sh
# @option -dropuse*|[`_choice_work_dropuse`]
_choice_work_dropuse() {
    _helper_work_json  | yq '(.Use // []) | .[].DiskPath'
}
```

> `*|` indicates that the option can occur multiple times and is separated by a "|" symbol.

```
$ go work edit -dropuse <tab>
./mymod1  ./mymod2  ./mymod3

$ go work edit -dropuse './mymod1|<tab>
./mymod2  ./mymod3
```

### Use `_argc_util_comp_multi`

```sh
# @option -type[`_choice_type`] <c>             File is of type c
_choice_type() {
    cat <<-'EOF' | _argc_util_comp_multi ,
b	block (buffered) special
c	character (unbuffered) special
d	directory
p	named pipe (FIFO)
f	regular file
l	symbolic link
s	socket
D	door (Solaris)
EOF
}
```

```
$ find . -type <tab>
b   c   d   ..


$ find . -type f,<tab>
b   c   d   ..
```

## Delegate to other command

```sh
# @arg cmd
# @arg args~[`_choice_args`]

_choice_args() {
    _argc_util_comp_subcommand 0
}
```

```
$ sudo ls --
```

```sh
# @arg workspace-name![`_choice_workspace`]
# @arg workspace-args~[`_choice_workspace_args`]

_choice_workspace_args() {
    (cd "$workspace" && _argc_util_comp_subcommand 1 yarn)
}
```

```
$ yarn <tab>
add   remove    ...

$ yarn workspace react <tab>
add   remove    ...
```

## Prefixed option

```sh
# @option -X-*[`_choice_option`]                pass additional options to JVM

_choice_option() {
    cat <<-'EOF' | _argc_util_comp_kv ':'
batch;;Disables background compilation.
bootclasspath=`_choice_boot_class_path`;;Specifies a list of directories
EOF
}
```

```
$ java -X<tab>
batch   bootclasspath:
```

## Symbol parameter

```sh
# @meta symbol +toolchain[`_choice_toolchain`]

_choice_toolchain() {
    echo table
    echo nightly
}
```

```
$ cargo +<tab>
table   nightly
```# Variables

Argc streamlines argument parsing in your shell scripts, allowing you to utilize variables seamlessly.

## Shell Variables

You can employ shell variables within your argc-based scripts just like you normally would in Bash. Argc doesn't interfere with their behavior.

```sh
# @cmd
cmd() {
  echo $1 $2  # Accessing positional arguments
  echo "$*"   # All arguments as a single string
  echo "$@"   # All arguments as separate strings
}
```

## Argc-Generated Variables

Argc automatically creates variables corresponding to the options, flags, and positional arguments defined in your script using the `@option`, `@flag`, and `@arg` directives.

```sh
# @option --oa
# @option --ob*  # Multiple values allowed
# @flag   --fa
# @arg va
# @arg vb*

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"  # Initializes Argc variables

echo '--oa:' $argc_oa
echo '--ob:' ${argc_ob[@]}  # Accessing multiple values as an array
echo '--fa:' $argc_fa
echo '  va:' $argc_va
echo '  vb:' ${argc_vb[@]}
```

Running `./script.sh --oa a --ob=b1 --ob=b2 --fa foo bar baz` would output:

```
--oa: a
--ob: b1 b2
--fa: 1
  va: foo
  vb: bar baz
```

## Built-in Variables

Argc also provides built-in variables that offer information about the parsing process:

*   **`argc__args`**: An array holding all command-line arguments.
*   **`argc__positionals`**: An array containing only the positional arguments.
*   **`argc__fn`**: The name of the function that will be executed.

**Additional Variables for Completion (Used internally by Argc-Completions):**

*   **`argc__cmd_arg_index`**: Index of the command argument within `argc__args`.
*   **`argc__cmd_fn`**: Name of the command function.
*   **`argc__dash`**: Index of the first em-dash (`--`) within the positional arguments.
*   **`argc__option`**: Variable name of the option currently being completed.

These variables are particularly useful when creating custom completion scripts. 

## Environment Variables

Several environment variables allow you to tailor Argc's behavior:

**User-Defined:**

*  **`ARGC_SHELL_PATH`**: Specifies the path to the shell/bash executable used by Argc.
*  **`ARGC_SCRIPT_NAME`**: Overrides the default script filename (Argcfile.sh).
*  **`ARGC_COMPGEN_DESCRIPTION`**: Disables descriptions for completion candidates if set to 0 or false. 
*  **`ARGC_COMPGEN_DESCRIPTION_MAX_WIDTH`**: Maximum width for completion descriptions; excess will be truncated with an ellipsis.
*  **`ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH`**: Defines the search path for Argc-based completion scripts.

**Argc-Injected:**

*  **`ARGC_PWD`**: Current working directory (available only in Argcfile.sh).

**Argc-Injected (for completion):**
*  **`ARGC_OS`**: Operating system type.
*  **`ARGC_COMPGEN`**: Indicates whether the script is being used for generating completion candidates (1) or not (0).
*  **`ARGC_CWORD`**: The last word in the processed command line.

It's important to distinguish between these two variables:

*  **`ARGC_CWORD`**: This variable isolates the final word, regardless of any preceding flags or options. For example, in the command `git --git-dir=git`, `ARGC_CWORD` would be `git`.
*  **`ARGC_LAST_ARG`**: This variable captures the entire last argument, including any flags or options attached to it. In the same example, `ARGC_LAST_ARG` would be `--git-dir=git`.

Understanding these variables is key to effectively leveraging Argc's capabilities and creating robust and user-friendly command-line interfaces.

`config get` now checks its key against the real resolved keys, and the same lookup gives tab-completion. `/tmp/argc/specification.md` confirmed the syntax: `[`fn`]` completes and validates, `[?`fn`]` only completes.

**Changes in `dash-skogai/bin/skogai`:**
- **`_choice_key`**: lists the resolved keys (`_resolve | cut -f1`). It respects `--file` and `--scope`, because argc fills in parsed flags before it calls a choice function.
  - **`get`**: uses it to validate, so `config get nope` now fails with argc's `invalid value` error and lists the possible keys.
  - **`set`**: uses it for completion only (`[?…]`), so you can still set new keys.
- **`_choice_target_key`**: lists only the keys in the layer `unset` would write to (local, `--global`, or `--file`'s `.local.md`), so completion only offers keys that can actually be removed.
- **Completion text**: shows each key's value, e.g. `base.test (true)`. These descriptions are only printed when `ARGC_COMPGEN=1`. Validation compares the whole line, description included, so printing them always broke `get`.
- **`config::get`**: is now a single lookup. I removed the old lowercasing, the `_`→`-` rewrite and the env fallback, since validation already guarantees a canonical key.

**Behaviour changes:**
- `config get STAGE.ON_STOP` and `config get stage.on_stop` used to work and are now rejected. You have to type the canonical key.
- A key that exists only as an env var, e.g. `SKOGAI_FOO_BAR` with no layer defining `foo.bar`, can no longer be read with `get`. The env name can't be reliably turned back into a key, so it can't be listed. Env overrides of keys that some layer defines still work.

I tested `get`, `get --show-origin`, completion for `get`/`set`/`unset`, and `set`/`unset` with `--global` and with `--file --scope`; all behaved as expected. One oddity: when completion has a single match (e.g. `set ev`), it shows no value description. I didn't look into why.

**Other ideas along the same lines, not done:**
- **One record type**: `_resolve` already produces `key\tvalue\torigin`. `get`, `list` and `env` could all be small views over it, e.g. a `_lookup key` helper instead of repeating `awk`/`cut`.
- **Shared options**: `--file`/`--scope` are declared on five subcommands. Moving them to the parent `config` command would cut that duplication, if argc passes parent options down the way you'd want.
- **`--scope` completion**: a `_choice_scope` could offer the top-level sections from `_resolve`.
- **Empty frontmatter key**: `_file_key`'s regex check happens after validation for `unset`, but `set` still needs it.

# config

a config is a [git config](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#_configuration_file) file of `section.key = value` pairs, read and written with `skogai-config`, registered as `argc config`.

## layers

folded in order, later wins:

1. **system**: `$SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR/config`, default `/etc/skogai/config`. the defaults; `config` in dash is installed here.
2. **global**: `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR/config`, default `~/.config/skogai/config`.
3. **local**: `$SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR/config`, default `.skogai/config`. a relative dir is from the git root, or pwd outside a repo.
4. **file**: with `--file x.md` (repeatable), the frontmatter of `x.md`, then of `x.local.md`. nested keys flatten to `a.b.c`, `_` reads as `-`, and `--scope s` mounts them under `s.`. needs `yq`.
5. **env**: key `a.b-c` reads env `SKOGAI_A_BC`, which overrides every layer. `.` is a relation and becomes `_`; `-` is part of a name and is dropped.

## commands

- `skogai-config get <key> [--show-origin] [--file x.md]... [--scope s]`: exit `1` if unset, `2` if a layer can't be read. a list prints one item per line.
- `skogai-config set <key> <value> [--global | --file x.md [--scope s]]`: writes local unless `--global`. `--file` writes `x.local.md`, never `x.md`; the value is read as yaml.
- `skogai-config unset <key> [--global | --file x.md [--scope s]]`
- `skogai-config list [--show-origin] [--file x.md]... [--scope s]`: a list prints one line per item.
- `skogai-config env [--file x.md]... [--scope s]`: the resolved config as `export` lines, for `mise` `_.source` or `eval`. a list's items are newline-separated.
- `skogai-config files [--file x.md]...`: the path of each layer, and whether it exists.

## merge

every key is replaced by the later layer. a key set twice in one layer resolves to its last value.

in a file layer, a frontmatter list is one value, replaced whole. `null` (`~`) removes the key, so it falls through to the default.

## keys

- `stage.on-stop`, `commit.on-stop`, `merge.on-stop`: git automation on stop.
- `stage.on-user-prompt-submit`, `commit.on-user-prompt-submit`, `merge.on-user-prompt-submit`: git automation on prompt submit.

# layout

- `./`: the meta top-layer, here we are creating for someone how we work on dash (CLAUDE.md, SKOGAI.md, TODO.md)
- `type/`: one file per type, each acting as a module
- `src/`: the future dot, an okn bundle. check with `okn validate src`
- `tmp/`: untyped or undecided

# design goals

skogai is functional: idempotent, immutable and strictly typed.

- **closed union**: a dot is a discriminated union of skogai types. okf `type` is the tag, dash defines the cases, and an unknown tag or untagged file is a type error.
- **layers, not inheritance**: the resolved state is `fold(merge, [base, global, local])`, later layer wins. no layer knows about the others.
- **git is the immutability model**: content is immutable, a change is a patch, history is the append-only log. types do not declare mutability.
- **refs resolve to commits**: a dot names dash by ref. every result reports the commit it resolved to, so it can be reproduced.
- **generated where possible**: a file derived from others (e.g. `DECISIONS.md`) is never hand-edited, and `check` regenerates and compares it.
- **pure by default**: only `apply` writes. see [skogai](type/tool/skogai.md).
- **don't rebuild okn**: list, validate, search and the rest belong to [okn](type/tool/okn.md).

# dash-skogai types

one section per type, in [type/index.md](type/index.md) order. each type says which files every instance of it **owns** (creates and manages, exactly one owner), **writes** (modifies without owning) and **watches** (reads, wants to know about changes). `<name>` in a path is the instance's name.

## type

a kind of thing, and the files each of its instances owns, writes and watches.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["type"])
  t -->|owns| p0["type/#lt;name#gt;.md"]
  t -->|owns| p1["type/#lt;name#gt;.schema.json"]
```

- **fields:** `type`, `title`, `description`, `fields`, `owns`, `writes`, `watches`
- **owns:** `type/<name>.md`, `type/<name>.schema.json`

a type defines a kind of thing. its definition is `type/<name>.md`, its instances live in `type/<name>/`, and `type/<name>.schema.json`, when there is one, is the schema for those instances. so [type.schema.json](type/type.schema.json) is the schema for every type definition.

### base

every instance of every type has the okf base. okf requires only `type`; the rest is optional:

- **identity**: `type`, `title`, `description`.
- **provenance**: `sources[]`, `usage_window`.
- **trust**: `generated: {by, at}`, `verified[]`.
- **lifecycle**: `status`, `stale_after`.

### definition

every type states:

- **type**: `type`.
- **title**: its name. instances carry it as their `type` in frontmatter.
- **fields**: the frontmatter every instance must have, beyond `type`.
- **owns**: the paths each instance creates and manages fully. every path has exactly one owner.
- **writes**: the paths each instance modifies without owning them.
- **watches**: the paths each instance reads and wants to know about when they change.

`<name>` in a path is the instance's name. a path ending in `/` is a folder.

### check

- a file with no owner is untyped: an error.
- a file with two owners is a conflict: an error.
- ownership is one step. `type` owns `type/tool.md`; `tool` owns `type/tool/gita.md`. `type` never owns what is under `type/tool/`.
- `writes` and `watches` can overlap freely.

`type` is itself a type: every `type/<name>.md` is an instance of it, including this file.

## decision

a choice and why it was made, written once.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["decision"])
  t -->|owns| p0["type/decision/#lt;nnnn#gt;-#lt;name#gt;.md"]
  t -.->|writes| p1["DECISIONS.md"]
```

- **fields:** `type`, `title`, `status`
- **owns:** `type/decision/<nnnn>-<name>.md`
- **writes:** `DECISIONS.md`

a decision records a choice and why. it is written once and never edited.

- **status**: `proposed`, `accepted` or `superseded`.
- **supersedes**: optional, the number of the decision this one replaces.

to change a decision, write a new one that supersedes it. `DECISIONS.md` is derived from the instances and never edited by hand.

## rule

a constraint that can be checked, enforcing a decision.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["rule"])
  t -->|owns| p0["type/rule/#lt;name#gt;.md"]
  t ==>|watches| p1["#lt;applies_to#gt;"]
```

- **fields:** `type`, `title`, `applies_to`
- **owns:** `type/rule/<name>.md`
- **watches:** `<applies_to>`

a rule is a decision made checkable.

- **applies_to**: the paths the rule constrains. the rule watches them and is re-checked when they change.
- **from**: optional, the decision it enforces.

a "we do X" that cannot be checked is a decision, not a rule.

## trigger

a script that runs when a file changes or an event happens.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["trigger"])
  t -->|owns| p0["type/trigger/#lt;name#gt;.md"]
  t -->|owns| p1["scripts/trigger/#lt;name#gt;.sh"]
  t ==>|watches| p2["#lt;when#gt;"]
```

- **fields:** `type`, `title`, `when`
- **owns:** `type/trigger/<name>.md`, `scripts/trigger/<name>.sh`
- **watches:** `<when>`

a trigger `<name>` owns:

- `type/trigger/<name>.md`: the instance.
- `scripts/trigger/<name>.sh`: what runs.

- **when**: the paths or events that run the script.

the base `watches` field is the simplest trigger: it marks interest in a path and runs nothing. a trigger adds the script.

## tool

an executable skogai uses, with its wrapper, scripts and workflow.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["tool"])

an event is something that happened, such as a turn ending or a tool about to run. each time it happens, one row is appended to the event log. rows are never edited; the log as a whole is temporary and can be deleted.

an event `<name>` owns:

- `type/event/<name>.md`: the instance. it says what happened and when it fires.
- `type/event/<name>.schema.json`: its rows. it narrows the row in [event.schema.json](type/event.schema.json) to this event's `input`.
- `scripts/event/<name>.sh`: what runs when it happens.

- **enabled**: optional. an event runs only when this is `true`. missing, or no instance at all, is off.

### the row

one json object per line in `.skogai/logs/event.jsonl`:

- **ts**: when it happened, utc, to the millisecond.
- **event**: the instance's `title`.
- **action**: optional, what the script did, when it did more than record the row.
- **input**: everything the event came with, unchanged. `$defs/input` in the schema lists the fields every event shares; `type/event/<name>.schema.json` adds its own and says which are required.

### the script

`scripts/event/<name>.sh` gets the event's `input` and appends exactly one row. it may answer: go on, stop with a reason, or a structured answer the event's source understands. when it can't run, it says so and lets the event go on, so a broken script never stops work.

### defaults

no event is on. the log path is the base config key `event.log-path`.

## definition

every type states:

- **type**: `type`.
- **title**: its name. instances carry it as their `type` in frontmatter.
- **fields**: the frontmatter every instance must have, beyond `type`.
- **owns**: the paths each instance creates and manages fully. every path has exactly one owner.
- **writes**: the paths each instance modifies without owning them.
- **watches**: the paths each instance reads and wants to know about when they change.

`<name>` in a path is the instance's name. a path ending in `/` is a folder.

## check

- a file with no owner is untyped: an error.
- a file with two owners is a conflict: an error.
- ownership is one step. `type` owns `type/tool.md`; `tool` owns `type/tool/gita.md`. `type` never owns what is under `type/tool/`.
- `writes` and `watches` can overlap freely.

`type` is itself a type: every `type/<name>.md` is an instance of it, including this file.

# skogai

the cli that turns dash into a dot. it is a function over values: `check` and `plan` are pure, and `apply` is the only writer.

## values

- **dash**: type definitions and functions, named by ref and resolved to a commit at use.
- **layers**: `base` (dash@ref), `global` (`~/.skogai`), `local` (`<repo>/.skogai`). key/value settings use [config](../config.md).
- **resolved**: `fold(merge, [base, global, local])`, later layer wins.
- **dot**: the resolved value written to disk, a closed union of skogai types.

## commands

### `skogai config`

implemented in `bin/skogai`. see [config](../config.md).

### `skogai check [<dot>]`

pure. reports type errors, writes nothing.

1. runs `okn validate` on the dot.
2. every file has exactly one owner (see [type](../type.md#check)).
3. every `type` tag is a case dash defines, and the file has that case's `fields`.
4. every derived file equals its regeneration.

prints the dash ref and the commit it resolved to.

### `skogai resolve [<dot>]`

pure. prints the resolved value, and for each entry the layer it came from.

### `skogai plan [<dot>]`

pure. prints the patch `apply` would make, as a git diff. an empty patch means the dot is already up to date.

### `skogai apply [<dot>] [<patch>]`

the only writer. applies `<patch>`, or the output of `plan` if none is given, with `git apply`.

- idempotent: after `apply`, `plan` is empty.
- init is `apply` on an empty dot.
- moving to a newer dash is changing the ref, then `plan` and `apply`.

## conventions

- `<dot>` defaults to `./.skogai`.
- output goes to stdout, diagnostics to stderr.
- exit `0`: clean or empty patch. `1`: type errors or a non-empty patch. `2`: usage or internal error.
- `--json` on every command, for machine output.
- anything okn already does (list, search, view, validate) is called through okn, not rebuilt.

   - a module that requires type offers `schema/<x>.json` (JSON Schema) in its files, and declares where instances live in its own config: `config.schema.<x>: <glob>`, glob relative to the local dir (.skogai), where `<key>` placeholders are filled from the same module's resolved config (e.g. `<dir>` -> value of `<module>.dir`).    - argc.sh commands: `skogai type check [module]...` (default: every module that requires type): for each schema, each instance file matching its glob: extract frontmatter with yq to json, validate with ajv (ajv is on PATH via mise; check its CLI, e.g. `ajv validate -s schema -d data --spec=draft2020` or whatever works; use the needed flags so it's quiet and strict about the schema). One line per problem `module<TAB>path<TAB>message`, exit 1 on any. A schema with no glob in config is an error. `skogai type ls [module]...`: module, schema name, glob, instance count.

tool_response.stdout:
# skogai modules

a module is one thing skogai can do, packaged so it can be found, run,
configured and copied into a repo as a unit. the argc script is one part of
it; the files it works with and its config defaults are the rest.

`skogai module check` enforces what this spec says a module must be.
`modules/core` and `modules/memory` are the reference modules.

## layout

```
<name>/
  module.md        required: manifest (frontmatter) and what it is (body)
  argc.sh          optional: the command, named by `command:`
  templates/ ...   optional: anything it offers, named by `files:`
  tests/*.bats     its own tests; not offered unless listed in `files:`
  module.local.md  local overrides, never shipped
```

the directory name is the module name.

## module.md

```markdown
---
type: module
name: memory
description: one fact per file, each with a stale_after; expired ones get decided on
command: argc.sh
tools: [yq]
requires: [core]
files:
  - templates/
config:
  dir: memory
  stale-days: 30
---

# memory

what it is, when to use it, what each config key means.
```

| field | | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | required | `module` | |
| `name` | required | string | lowercase, one segment (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`), same as the directory |
| `description` | required | string | one line, what it is; shown by `module ls` |
| `command` | optional | path | its argc script, relative to the module dir; `skogai <name>` runs it |
| `tools` | optional | list | executables it needs on `PATH` |
| `requires` | optional | list | modules it needs; every module but `core` requires `core` |
| `files` | optional | list | paths it offers beyond `module.md` and `command`; a path ending in `/` is a whole directory |
| `config` | optional | map | config defaults, read as `<name>.<key>` |

a module consists of exactly `module.md`, `command` and `files`. nothing else
is copied on install; anything else in the directory is the source's own.

the body is prose for humans and agents: what the module is, every config key
and what it means, and anything a user decides when installing it.

## names

- `core`, `config`, `module` and `help` are reserved: `skogai config ...` is
  always core.
- config keys are lowercase; `.` is a relation and `-` is part of a name, so
  `memory.stale-days` is `SKOGAI_MEMORY_STALEDAYS` as env.

## where modules are found

in this order, the first module by a name wins:

| layer | where |
|---|---|
| `local` | `.skogai/modules/` at the git root (or `$SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR/modules`) |
| `global` | `~/.config/skogai/modules/` (or `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR/modules`) |
| `source` | each dir on `$SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH`, by default the plugin's `modules/` |

a module runs from wherever it is found; installing is not needed to use it.
an installed copy shadows its source, a local one shadows a global one.

## installing

installing copies a module into `local` or `global` so it can be edited there.
it is an offer, never a takeover:

- `skogai module add <name|path>` prints the plan, one line per file: `add`
  (missing, will copy), `same`, or `keep` (there and different, never
  overwritten). it exits `1` if anything would be added.
- `--apply` copies. `--to local|global` picks the layer, default
  `core.module.install`.
- `skogai module diff <name>` shows how an installed copy differs from its source.
- nothing outside `.skogai/` (local) or `~/.config/skogai/` (global) is written.

## config

a module's keys live under its name. the layers, later wins:

1. `config:` in every found `module.md` (defaults)
2. system, global, local: git-config files `config` in `/etc/skogai`,
   `~/.config/skogai`, `.skogai`
3. `config:` in each module's `module.local.md`
4. `--file` layers (`skogai config` only)
5. `SKOGAI_*` env

`skogai config set --module <name> <name>.<key> <value>` writes a module's
`module.local.md`: beside an installed copy's `module.md`, and for a source
module in `.skogai/modules/<name>/`, never into the source.
`skogai config get <key> --show-origin` says which layer won.

## skogai

`skogai` is the runner; argc is the engine under it.

- in Claude Code sessions it is this plugin's `bin/skogai`, on the Bash tool's
  `PATH` while the plugin is enabled. it finds modules when it runs, so
  nothing needs registering. its `SessionStart` hook runs
  `skogai module build --to global` and puts the built `skogai` first on
  the Bash tool's `PATH` (via `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`), so `skogai --help` lists
  every module found from where the session started.
- in a shell, `skogai module build` generates a static `skogai`: one argc
  file with a forwarding recipe for core's groups and every module found
  from there, so `--help`, completion and man pages cover all of them. every
  run still goes through the `bin/skogai` that built it, and a module found
  after the build runs too, only without help and completion. the build is
  throwaway, in `.skogai/tmp/skogai/` (or the global dir's): `bin/`,
  `man/man1/`, `completions/skogai.sh` for `ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH`, and
  `completions/skogai.{bash,zsh,fish}`. it prints the env lines for
  `PATH`, `MANPATH` and `ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH`; putting them in a shell, a
  `.envrc` or mise is up to the user. the first build runs the checkout's
  `bin/skogai` by path.
- `skogai module sandbox [dir]` (default `$TMPDIR/skogai`) is an empty
  skogai to try things in: `system/` and `global/` layers, a git repo
  `repo/` with every module found from here installed in its `.skogai/modules`
  (from its source when it has one) and `skogai` built there. it prints the
  env lines that switch a shell into it (`eval "$(skogai module sandbox)"`,
  fish `skogai module sandbox | source`): no `SKOGAI_*` config from outside,
  the three layer dirs, the built `skogai` on `PATH`, `cd repo`. it also
  writes `<dir>/run`, the same switch for one command (`/tmp/skogai/run
  skogai memory ls`, a shell with none), for callers whose env does not
  persist between commands, like an agent's Bash tool. rerunning replaces
  it; a dir it did not make is refused.

## the command

an argc script. `skogai <name> <args>` runs it with `argc --argc-run` from the
caller's directory, with this env (`skogai module env <name>`):

| var | |
|---|---|
| `SKOGAI_MODULE` | its name |
| `SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR` | its directory, wherever it was found; its `files:` are here |
| `SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR` | the local `.skogai`, absolute |
| `SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR` | the global dir, absolute |
| `SKOGAI_<NAME>_<KEY>` | each of its own resolved config keys |

rules:

- read paths and config from that env, never from `$PWD` or its own location.
  start with `: "${SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR:?run me as \`skogai <name>\`}"`.
- `# @meta binname skogai <name>` so help and man pages read right;
  `# @meta require-tools` matches `tools:`.
- a positional `~` argument takes everything after it, flags included: put
  options before it.
- exit `0` ok, `1` a finding or an unapplied change (like `diff`), `2` usage.
- pure by default: a recipe that changes an existing file takes `--apply` and
  without it prints what it would do. creating a new file is fine; overwriting
  one is refused.
- don't name a recipe after a bash builtin (`eval`, `cd`, `exec`, `set`); argc's
  generated code calls them. group them instead (`config::set`).
- other modules are called as `skogai <other> ...`, never by path.

## tests

bats. `skogai module test [name]...` runs, for each module:

1. the contract, core's `tests/contract.bats`: `module check` has no errors,
   `--help` exits 0, the command refuses to run outside `skogai`, every
   `config:` default resolves under its name, `module env` is right, `add` is
   a plan and `--apply` installs, and the installed copy passes check and runs.
2. its own `tests/*.bats`, from its source when it has one.

a test file starts with `load "$SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER"` (core's
`tests/helper.bash`). every test then runs in an empty git repo
(`$REPO`, with `$LOCAL` its `.skogai`) with its own system and global layers
and no `SKOGAI_*` config from the caller, so nothing outside
`BATS_TEST_TMPDIR` is touched. the module under test is a source there.
helpers: `skogai`, `module_dir`, `module_field`, `assert_status`,
`assert_output_has`, `refute_output_has`, `assert_file`. a file with its own
`setup()` calls `skogai_setup` first.

set state the way a user would (`skogai config set`, `skogai module add`),
not by writing layer files.

## creating one

1. `skogai module new <name> "<description>"` scaffolds `module.md`, a
   hello-world `argc.sh` and `tests/<name>.bats` in `.skogai/modules/<name>/`
   (`--to global` for `~/.config/skogai/modules/`).
2. fill in `module.md`: `tools`, `files`, `config` defaults, and a body that
   explains every key.
3. write the recipes in `argc.sh` (argc spec: core's `docs/argc/specification.md`).
4. write its tests, then `skogai module test <name>`: the contract and its
   own tests pass.
5. to ship it with a plugin, move the directory to the plugin's `modules/`.
   it is then a `source` everywhere the plugin is enabled.

# what every module is held to, run for each by `skogai module test`
# with SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE set. the spec is docs/module.md.

load "$SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER"

@test "contract: module check has no errors" {
    run skogai module check "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 0
}

@test "contract: --help exits 0" {
    [[ -n $(module_field .command) ]] || skip "no command"
    run skogai "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE" --help
    assert_status 0
}

@test "contract: the command refuses to run outside skogai" {
    [[ -n $(module_field .command) ]] || skip "no command"
    [[ $SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE != core ]] || skip "core is what runs modules"
    local cmd
    cmd="$(module_dir)/$(module_field .command)"
    run argc --argc-run "$cmd" "$(argc --argc-export "$cmd" | yq -p json '.subcommands[0].name')"
    [[ $status -ne 0 ]]
}

@test "contract: config defaults resolve under its name" {
    local key
    while IFS= read -r key; do
        [[ -n $key ]] || continue
        run skogai config get "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE.$key" --show-origin
        assert_status 0
        assert_output_has "module:$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    done < <(yq --front-matter=extract '.config // {} | .. | select(tag != "!!map") | path | .[1:] | join(".")' "$(module_dir)/module.md")

@test "contract: module env names it and its dir" {
    run skogai module env "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 0
    assert_output_has "export SKOGAI_MODULE=$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_output_has "export SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR=$(module_dir)"
    assert_output_has "export SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR=$LOCAL"
}

@test "contract: add is a plan, --apply installs, a second add is all same" {
    run skogai module add "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 1
    [[ ! -e $LOCAL/modules/$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE ]]
    run skogai module add "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE" --apply
    assert_status 0
    assert_file "$LOCAL/modules/$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE/module.md"
    run skogai module add "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 0
    refute_output_has "add "
    refute_output_has "keep "
}

@test "contract: the installed copy passes check and runs" {
    skogai module add "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE" --apply 2>/dev/null >/dev/null
    run skogai module show "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_output_has "local	$LOCAL/modules/$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    run skogai module check "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 0
    [[ -n $(yq --front-matter=extract '.command // ""' "$LOCAL/modules/$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE/module.md") ]] || return 0
    run skogai "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE" --help
    assert_status 0
}
# the base every module's tests stand on: `load "$SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER"` at the
# top of a .bats file. each test gets an empty git repo as its cwd and its own
# system, global and local layers, so nothing outside BATS_TEST_TMPDIR is
# read or written. a file that defines its own setup() calls skogai_setup.
#
# set by `skogai module test`: SKOGAI_BIN, SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH,
# SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE (the module under test), SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER (this file).

skogai_setup() {
    local v
    # run --separate-stderr
    bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    # config from the caller's env would shadow every layer
    for v in $(compgen -e SKOGAI_); do
        case "$v" in SKOGAI_BIN | SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH | SKOGAI_TEST_*) ;; *) unset "$v" ;; esac
    done
    export SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/system"
    export SKOGAI_CONFIG_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/global"
    REPO="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/repo"
    LOCAL="$REPO/.skogai"
    mkdir -p "$REPO"
    cd "$REPO" || return 1
    git init -q
}

setup() { skogai_setup; }

# modules call `skogai <other>`, so it is on PATH as well
PATH="$(dirname "$SKOGAI_BIN"):$PATH"
skogai() { "$SKOGAI_BIN" "$@"; }

# the source dir of the module under test, or of $1
module_dir() { skogai module show "${1:-$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE}" | awk -F"\t" "NR == 1 { print \$2 }"; }

# a manifest field of the module under test, empty if missing
module_field() { yq --front-matter=extract "$1 // \"\"" "$(module_dir)/module.md"; }

assert_status() {
    [[ $status -eq $1 ]] || { printf 'expected exit %s, got %s\n%s\n' "$1" "$status" "$output" >&2; return 1; }
}

assert_output_has() {
    [[ $output == *"$1"* ]] || { printf 'output lacks: %s\n---\n%s\n' "$1" "$output" >&2; return 1; }
}

refute_output_has() {
    [[ $output != *"$1"* ]] || { printf 'output has: %s\n---\n%s\n' "$1" "$output" >&2; return 1; }
}

assert_file() { [[ -f $1 ]] || { echo "no file: $1" >&2; return 1; }; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe memory: one fact per file, each with a stale_after; expired ones get decided on
# @meta require-tools yq
# @meta binname skogai memory

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval, SKOGAI_* by `skogai module env`
set -euo pipefail

: "${SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR:?run me as \`skogai memory\`}"
DIR="$SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR/$SKOGAI_MEMORY_DIR"
INDEX="$DIR/$SKOGAI_MEMORY_INDEX"
# field separator of _entries: not whitespace, so an empty field survives `read`
FS=$'\x1f'

# @cmd every entry: stale_after, name, description; `!` marks one that is due (expired, or no stale_after)
ls() {
    local name stale desc
    while IFS="$FS" read -r name stale desc; do
        printf '%s %-10s %-36s %s\n' "$([[ $stale == none || $stale < $(date +%F) ]] && echo '!' || echo ' ')" "$stale" "$name" "$desc"
    done < <(_entries)
}

# @cmd entries that are due, oldest first, as name<TAB>stale_after<TAB>description; exit 1 if there are any
stale() {
    local today out
    today="$(date +%F)"
    out="$(_entries | awk -F"$FS" -v OFS='\t' -v t="$today" '$2 == "none" || $2 < t { $1 = $1; print }' | sort -t$'\t' -k2)"
    [[ -n $out ]] || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
    return 1
}

# @cmd write a new entry from templates/entry.md; refuses an existing name
# @arg name!  lowercase, `-` inside a name
# @arg description!  one line, used for recall
# @option --days  days until stale, default memory.stale-days
new() {
    [[ $argc_name =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || { echo "bad name: $argc_name" >&2; return 2; }
    local file="$DIR/$argc_name.md"
    [[ ! -e $file ]] || { echo "exists: $file" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$DIR"
    NAME="$argc_name" DESC="$argc_description" CREATED="$(date +%F)" \
        STALE="$(date -d "+${argc_days:-$SKOGAI_MEMORY_STALEDAYS} days" +%F)" \
        awk '{ gsub(/\{\{name\}\}/, ENVIRON["NAME"]); gsub(/\{\{description\}\}/, ENVIRON["DESC"])
               gsub(/\{\{created\}\}/, ENVIRON["CREATED"]); gsub(/\{\{stale_after\}\}/, ENVIRON["STALE"]); print }' \
        "$SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR/templates/entry.md" >"$file"
    echo "wrote $file" >&2
    echo "not in the index yet: skogai memory index --apply" >&2
}

# @cmd index lines for entries missing from the index, and index links to missing files. pure unless --apply
#
# exit 1 when something is out of sync and --apply was not given.
# --apply appends the missing lines; dead links are only reported.
# @flag --apply  append the missing lines to the index
index() {
    local name stale desc missing=() rc=0 link
    while IFS="$FS" read -r name stale desc; do
        grep -qF "($name.md)" "$INDEX" 2>/dev/null || missing+=("* [$name]($name.md) - $desc")
    done < <(_entries)
    while IFS= read -r link; do
        [[ -f $DIR/$link ]] || { echo "dead link: $link" >&2; rc=1; }
    done < <(grep -o '([^)]*\.md)' "$INDEX" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '()')
    [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]] || return "$rc"
    printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}"
    if [[ ${argc_apply:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" >>"$INDEX"
        echo "appended ${#missing[@]} to $INDEX" >&2
        return "$rc"
    fi
    return 1
}

# "name FS stale_after FS description" per entry, the index excluded; a missing stale_after is `none`
_entries() {
    local f
    for f in "$DIR"/*.md; do
        [[ -f $f && $f != "$INDEX" ]] || continue
        FS="$FS" yq --front-matter=extract -r '[.name // "", .stale_after // .metadata.stale_after // "none", .description // ""] | join(strenv(FS))' "$f"
    done
}

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

---
type: module
name: runner
description: typed io for handing work to agents, prompt + files -> json matching a schema
command: argc.sh
tools: [jq, yq, git, claude]
requires: [core]
files:

config:

  journal: journal.md
---

# runner

every agent call is one function:

```
send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json
```

files are inlined as `<file path>` blocks, the worker gets no tools unless
`--tools` says so, and stdout is the json object (`.structured_output` of
`claude -p --json-schema`). envelopes are logged to `.skogai/logs/runner/`.

| recipe | use |
|---|---|
| `send -p <q> -f <file>... -s answer` | one bounded question, short checkable answer |
| `send -s check -f <file>...` | findings as `{path, line, rule, severity, message}` |
| `improve [-f file]... [--apply] <request>` | whole-file edits from a worker, patch derived with `diff -u`; prints it unless `--apply` |
| `wo new <name> -s <schema> -f <file>...` | write `.skogai/workorders/<name>.md` |
| `wo run <name> [--sandbox]` | run it, result in `<name>.result.json`; `--sandbox` runs the worker in a fresh sandbox |
| `wo ls` | workorders and whether they have a result |
| `journal prompts [file] [--last N] [--md]` | only the user's input from a journal, one json row per turn |
| `journal harvest [file] [--last N] [--turns N]` | workers pick decisions, docs, todos, learnings out of a journal |

exit `0` ok or empty patch, `1` agent error or a patch printed but not
applied, `2` usage.

## workorders

one bounded question per workorder. inputs are listed as files, never "go look
around". output is a schema, so the result is checkable without reading prose.
`files:` are relative to the repo root.

```markdown
---
type: workorder
title: <name>
schema: answer
tools: ""
allow: []
sandbox: true
files:
  - path/to/input.md
---

<one bounded question>
```

`allow:` are tool patterns the worker may use without asking (`send --allow`);
the worker runs with `--permission-mode dontAsk`, so a tool in `tools` that no
pattern allows is denied.

`sandbox: true` (or `wo run --sandbox`) runs the worker inside a fresh
`skogai module sandbox` at `.skogai/tmp/sandbox/<name>`: cwd the sandbox repo,
skogai config the sandbox's layers, every module found from here installed.
a worker with `tools` then tries skogai things there, not in this tree or with
this config. inputs are still inlined from here. the sandbox is kept after the
run for a look, and replaced by the next one.

## config

| key | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `runner.model` | `sonnet` | model for every agent call without `--model` |
| `runner.journal` | `journal.md` | the session journal, relative to `.skogai/` |

## schemas

`schemas/*.json`, named by `--schema` (or a path): `answer`, `check`, `edit`
(what `improve` asks for), `harvest`. a new one is small,
`additionalProperties: false`, every field required.

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line

# @cmd run modules' tests with bats: core's contract, then the module's own tests/
#
# the contract (core's tests/contract.bats) runs for every module; its own
# tests/*.bats load core's tests/helper.bash for an isolated repo and layers.
# tests, and core's contract and helper, come from the source when there is one, else where it is found.
# @arg module*[`_choice_module`]  default every module found
# @option --filter  only tests whose name matches this regex
module::test() {
    : "${SKOGAI_BIN:?run me as skogai module test}"
    command -v bats >/dev/null || { echo "bats is not on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }
    local core name dir rc=0 files names=("${argc_module[@]}")
    core="$(_source core)" || IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ core < <(_module core)
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_modules | cut -f1)
    for name in "${names[@]}"; do
        dir="$(_source "$name")" || IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$name") ||
            { echo "no module: $name" >&2; rc=1; continue; }
        files=("$core/tests/contract.bats")
        [[ ! -d $dir/tests ]] || mapfile -t -O 1 files < <(find "$dir/tests" -name '*.bats' ! -path "$core/tests/contract.bats" | sort)
        echo "# $name" >&2
        # the module under test is a source in its isolated repo, wherever it was found
        SKOGAI_MODULE_PATH="$(dirname "$dir"):$MODULE_PATH" \
            SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE="$name" SKOGAI_TEST_HELPER="$core/tests/helper.bash" \
            bats ${argc_filter:+--filter "$argc_filter"} "${files[@]}" || rc=1
    done
    return "$rc"

# one line per problem: name, error or warn, message. exit 1 on any error;
# a missing tool is a warn, it is about this machine, not the module.
# @arg module*[?`_choice_module`]  names, or paths to module dirs
module::check() {
    local m dir rc=0 targets=("${argc_module[@]}")
    [[ ${#targets[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t targets < <(_modules | cut -f3)
    for m in "${targets[@]}"; do
        if [[ $m == */* || $m == . ]]; then

# SKOGAI_RUNNER_MODEL.
# @arg name![`_choice_module`]
module::env() {
    local dir key value
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _ _ dir < <(_module "$argc_name") || exit 1

# a module dir to install from: a path, or a name looked up in the sources only
_source() {
    local p
    if [[ $1 == */* || $1 == . ]]; then
        p="$(cd "${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}" && realpath -e "$1")" && [[ -f $p/module.md ]] && echo "$p"
        return
    fi
    _module_bases | while IFS=$'\t' read -r layer p; do
        [[ $layer == source && -f $p/$1/module.md ]] && { realpath "$p/$1"; break; }
    done | grep .

# files a module consists of, relative to its dir: module.md, its command, its `files:`
_module_files() {
    local dir="$1" f
    {
        echo module.md
        _field "$dir/module.md" .command
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            [[ -n $f ]] || continue
            if [[ -d $dir/$f ]]; then (cd "$dir" && find "${f%/}" -type f); else echo "$f"; fi
        done < <(_field "$dir/module.md" '.files[]')
    } | grep . | sort -u

# the main argc file for `module build`: templates/main.sh with one forwarding
# recipe per core group and per module with a command between its markers
_main() {
    local tpl name layer dir cmd desc known=config\|module\|help
    tpl="$(dirname "$SELF")/templates/main.sh"
    sed '/^# >>> generated$/q' "$tpl"
    printf 'BIN=%q\nCORE=%q\ndeclare -A CMDS=()\n' "$SKOGAI_BIN" "$SELF"
    for name in config module; do
        desc="$(argc --argc-export "$SELF" | N="$name" yq -p json '.subcommands[] | select(.name == strenv(N)) | .describe | split("\n") | .[0]')"
        _forward "$name" "$desc"
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ $name != core ]] || continue
        cmd="$(module::command_of "$dir")" || continue
        printf 'CMDS[%s]=%q\n' "$name" "$cmd"
        _forward "$name" "$(_field "$dir/module.md" .description)"
        known+="|$name"
    done < <(_modules)
    printf 'KNOWN=%q\n' "$known"
    sed -n '/^# <<< generated$/,$p' "$tpl"

# one forwarding recipe: help and completion from the real script, the run through $BIN
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # generated code, expanded when it runs
_forward() {
    printf '\n# @cmd %s\n# @arg args~[?`_choice_forward`]\n' "$2"
    printf '%s() { exec "$BIN" %s "${argc_args[@]}"; }\n\n' "$1" "$1"

# names a module can't have: `skogai <name>` would be core's
_reserved() { [[ $1 =~ ^(core|config|module|help)$ ]]; }

# spec problems of one module dir as "name<TAB>error|warn<TAB>message"; 1 on any error
_check() {
    local dir="$1" md="$1/module.md" name f t r err=0
    name="$(basename "$dir")"
    _bad() { printf '%s\terror\t%s\n' "$name" "$1"; err=1; }
    [[ -f $md ]] || { _bad "no module.md"; return 1; }
    yq --front-matter=extract 'select(document_index == 0) | tag == "!!map"' "$md" 2>/dev/null | grep -qx true ||
        { _bad "module.md has no frontmatter map"; return 1; }
    [[ $(_field "$md" .type) == module ]] || _bad "type is not module"
    [[ $(_field "$md" .name) == "$name" ]] || _bad "name is not the directory name ($name)"
    [[ $name =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || _bad "name is not lowercase, one segment"
    [[ $name == core ]] || ! _reserved "$name" || _bad "name is reserved"
    [[ -n $(_field "$md" .description) && $(_field "$md" .description | wc -l) == 1 ]] || _bad "description is not one line"
    f="$(_field "$md" .command)"
    if [[ -n $f ]]; then
        if [[ ! -f $dir/$f ]]; then
            _bad "command $f is missing"
        else
            argc --argc-export "$dir/$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _bad "command $f does not parse with argc"
        fi
    fi
    for t in tools requires files; do
        [[ $(yq --front-matter=extract ".$t | tag" "$md") =~ ^\!\!(seq|null)$ ]] || _bad "$t is not a list"
    done
    [[ $(yq --front-matter=extract '.config | tag' "$md") =~ ^\!\!(map|null)$ ]] || _bad "config is not a map"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        [[ -z $f || -e $dir/$f ]] || _bad "file $f is missing"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.files[]')
    [[ $name == core ]] || _field "$md" '.requires[]' | grep -qx core || _bad "does not require core"
    while IFS= read -r r; do
        [[ -z $r ]] || _module "$r" >/dev/null || _bad "requires $r, not found"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.requires[]')
    while IFS= read -r t; do
        [[ -z $t ]] || command -v "$t" >/dev/null || printf '%s\twarn\ttool %s not on PATH\n' "$name" "$t"
    done < <(_field "$md" '.tools[]')
    compgen -G "$dir/tests/*.bats" >/dev/null || printf '%s\twarn\tno tests/*.bats\n' "$name"
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        printf '%s\twarn\tunknown field %s\n' "$name" "$f"
    done < <(yq --front-matter=extract 'keys | .[] | select(test("^(type|name|description|command|tools|requires|files|config)$") | not)' "$md")

_missing() {

    while IFS= read -r t; do
        [[ -z $t ]] || command -v "$t" >/dev/null || echo "missing tool: $t"
    done < <(_field "$1/module.md" '.tools[]')
    while IFS= read -r r; do
        [[ -z $r ]] || _module "$r" >/dev/null || echo "missing module: $r (skogai module add $r)"

_present() { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$([[ -f $2 ]] && echo present || echo missing)"; }

_layer_file() {

    system) echo "$SKOGAI_SYSTEM_DIR/config" ;;
    global) echo "$GLOBAL_DIR/config" ;;
    local) echo "$(_local_dir)/config" ;;

_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# go in the local install dir, never into the source
_module_local_md() {

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
    local f
    for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do

        _local_md "$f"

# set/unset into a markdown file: sets `file`, and `argc_scope` for --module
_md_target() {
    if [[ -n ${argc_module:-} ]]; then
        local layer dir
        IFS=$'\t' read -r _ layer dir < <(_module "$argc_module") || { echo "no module: $argc_module" >&2; exit 2; }
        file="$(_module_local_md "$argc_module" "$layer" "$dir")"
        argc_scope="$argc_module"
        MD_ROOT=config
        return 0
    fi

    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
    local k="${1^^}"
    k="${k//-/}"
    echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under the scope ($2, or --scope) if given, with `_` read as `-`.
# $3 picks the map to read, default the whole frontmatter. a list is one value,
# its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
    yq --front-matter=extract "select(document_index == 0) | ${3:-.} // {}" "$1" |
        SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${2-${argc_scope:-}}" yq '
        select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")'
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
    local -A val origin
    local layer file key value env tag name dir fm entry
    _fold() { # file scope root origin
        [[ -f $1 ]] || return 0
        fm="$(_frontmatter "$1" "$2" "$3")" || exit 2
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
            [[ -n $key ]] || continue
            if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
                builtin unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
            else
                val[$key]="$value"
                origin[$key]="$4"
            fi
        done <<<"$fm"
    }
    local mods
    mods="$(_modules)"
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$dir/module.md" "$name" .config "module:$name"
    done <<<"$mods"
    for layer in system global local; do
        file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
        [[ -f $file ]] || continue
        while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
            key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
            value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
            [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
            val[$key]="$value"
            origin[$key]="$layer"
        done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
    done
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r name layer dir; do
        [[ -z $name ]] || _fold "$(_module_local_md "$name" "$layer" "$dir")" "$name" .config "module:$name.local"
    done <<<"$mods"
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        _fold "$file" "${argc_scope:-}" . "file:$file"
    done < <(_file_layers)
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        env="$(_env_name "$key")"
        if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
            val[$key]="${!env}"
            origin[$key]="env:$env"
        fi
    done
    for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
    done | sort
}

_target_file() {
    if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# every resolved key, only --module's own if given; choices for get and set,
# described by value when completing
_choice_key() {
    local keys
    keys="$(_resolve | awk -F'\t' -v m="${argc_module:-}" 'm == "" || index($1, m ".") == 1')"
    if [[ ${ARGC_COMPGEN:-0} == 1 ]]; then cut -f1,2 <<<"$keys" | tr "$SEP" ' '; else cut -f1 <<<"$keys"; fi
}

# type

a module that requires `type` says what its files look like: each
`schema/<x>.json` it offers (JSON Schema 2020-12) is checked against the
frontmatter of every instance, the files its config key `<module>.schema.<x>`
globs.

```markdown
---
name: memory
requires: [core, type]
files:
  - schema/
config:
  dir: memory
  schema:
    entry: <dir>/*.md
---
```

the glob is relative to the local dir (`.skogai`). `<key>` in it is the same
module's resolved `<module>.<key>`: with the above `<dir>/*.md` is
`.skogai/memory/*.md`, and moves when `memory.dir` does. a schema with no glob
is an error.

| command | |
|---|---|
| `check [module]...` | every instance against its schema, one line per problem: `module<TAB>path<TAB>message`; exit 1 on any |
| `ls [module]...` | `module<TAB>schema<TAB>glob<TAB>instances` |

without a module both take every module that requires `type`. frontmatter is
read with `yq`, validated with `ajv --spec=draft2020 --strict=true`, so a
schema with an unknown keyword is a problem too.

## tests

`tests/contract.bats` runs against every module that requires `type`: each
`schema/*.json` compiles, each has a glob, and `skogai type check <module>`
passes in a fresh repo.

tool_response.stdout:
`skogai` is the runner, argc the engine under it. everything it does is a module.

- `docs/module.md`: the spec. a module is a dir with a `module.md` (command, tools, requires, files, config defaults) and usually an argc script; `skogai <name>` runs it with its env.
- `bin/skogai`: on the Bash tool's `PATH` in sessions. dispatches to modules found at run time; anything else goes to core.
- `modules/core`: config across layers, and `skogai module ls|show|check|test|build|add|diff|new|env`. owns the test base (`tests/helper.bash`, `tests/contract.bats`), the templates and the argc docs (`docs/argc/`).
- `modules/runner`: typed agent io, `send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json`, plus `improve`, `wo`, `journal`.
- `modules/memory`: `.skogai/memory/`, the worked example of a small module.
- the marketplace repo's own `.skogai/modules/marketplace`: plugin recipes, a local module, so it exists only in that repo.
- skills `module` (use and create modules) and `runner` (delegate work).

## decisions

- **modules, not scripts**: a module is the argc script plus the files it works with and its config defaults, copied into `.skogai/` as a unit. found local, then global, then sources; runs from wherever found.
- **skogai is the runner**: no `~/Argcfile.sh` and no registry. `bin/skogai` resolves modules dynamically; `skogai module build` generates the static file a shell needs for help, completion and man pages (the old-core build trick, `ARGC_COMPLETIONS_PATH` instead of a completions repo entry).
- **a module reads its world from env**: `SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR`, `SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR`, `SKOGAI_<NAME>_<KEY>`. no lookups of its own; it refuses to run outside `skogai`.
- **core sets the test base**: every module is held to the contract, then its own tests, all isolated from the caller's config.
- **pure by default**: `improve`, `module add`, `memory index` print a plan and exit `1`; only `--apply` writes. scaffolds create new files and refuse to overwrite.
- **whole files, derived patch**: workers return complete files (schema `edit`), the runner builds the diff with `diff -u`. paths not handed over are refused.
- **no tools by default**: inputs are inlined as `<file path>` blocks. `--tools` opts in.
- **installing is an offer**: changed installed files are kept, `module diff` shows how.
