#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe type: instance schemas, every module's schema/<x>.json checked against its instances
#
# a module that requires type offers schema/<x>.json and globs its instances
# with config <module>.schema.<x>, relative to the local dir; `<key>` in the
# glob is the module's own resolved <module>.<key>.
# @meta require-tools yq,ajv
# @meta binname skogai type

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval, SKOGAI_* by `skogai module env`
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s globstar

: "${SKOGAI_MODULE_DIR:?run me as \`skogai type\`}"
AJV=(--spec=draft2020 --strict=true)
# field separator of _schemas: not whitespace, so an empty field survives `read`
FS=$'\x1f'

# @cmd every instance against its schema; one line per problem: module<TAB>path<TAB>message
#
# exit 1 on any problem: an instance that does not match, frontmatter that
# does not parse, a schema that does not compile, a schema with no glob.
# @arg module*[`_choice_typed`]  default every module that requires type
check() {
    local m schema glob problem f rc=0 tmp
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' RETURN
    while IFS="$FS" read -r m schema glob problem; do
        [[ -z $problem ]] || { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$m" "$schema" "$problem"; rc=1; continue; }
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            _validate "$m" "$schema" "$f" "$tmp/data.json" || rc=1
        done < <(_instances "$glob")
    done < <(_schemas)
    return "$rc"
}

# @cmd each schema: module<TAB>schema<TAB>glob<TAB>instances
#
# a schema with no glob goes to stderr as module<TAB>path<TAB>message, exit 1.
# @arg module*[`_choice_typed`]  default every module that requires type
ls() {
    local m schema glob problem rc=0
    while IFS="$FS" read -r m schema glob problem; do
        [[ -z $problem ]] || { printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$m" "$schema" "$problem" >&2; rc=1; continue; }
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$m" "$(basename "$schema" .json)" "$glob" "$(_instances "$glob" | grep -c . || true)"
    done < <(_schemas)
    return "$rc"
}

# "module FS schema path FS filled glob FS problem" for each schema of the
# given modules, the problem empty unless there is no glob
_schemas() {
    local m dir schema x glob mods=("${argc_module[@]}")
    [[ ${#mods[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t mods < <(_typed)
    for m in "${mods[@]}"; do
        dir="$(_dir "$m")" || { printf '%s\x1f-\x1f\x1fno module\n' "$m"; continue; }
        for schema in "$dir"/schema/*.json; do
            [[ -f $schema ]] || continue
            x="$(basename "$schema" .json)"
            if ! glob="$(skogai config get "$m.schema.$x" 2>/dev/null)" || [[ -z $glob ]]; then
                printf '%s\x1f%s\x1f\x1fno glob: config %s.schema.%s\n' "$m" "$schema" "$m" "$x"
            elif ! glob="$(_fill "$m" "$glob")"; then
                printf '%s\x1f%s\x1f\x1f%s\n' "$m" "$schema" "$glob"
            else
                printf '%s\x1f%s\x1f%s\x1f\n' "$m" "$schema" "$glob"
            fi
        done
    done
}

# the glob with each `<key>` replaced by the module's <module>.<key>; on a
# missing key prints the problem and returns 1
_fill() {
    local rest="$2" out="" v
    while [[ $rest =~ ^([^\<]*)\<([a-z0-9.-]+)\>(.*)$ ]]; do
        v="$(skogai config get "$1.${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "no config $1.${BASH_REMATCH[2]} for <${BASH_REMATCH[2]}>"; return 1; }
        out+="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$v"
        rest="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
    done

# files the glob matches, relative to the local dir, sorted
_instances() {
    local f
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        [[ -f $f ]] && echo "$f"
    done < <(compgen -G "$SKOGAI_LOCAL_DIR/$1" | sort || true)
}

# one instance's frontmatter against a schema, problems as lines
_validate() {
    local m="$1" schema="$2" f="$3" json="$4" err line
    if ! err="$(yq --front-matter=extract -o json 'select(document_index == 0)' "$f" 2>&1 >"$json")"; then
        printf '%s\t%s\tfrontmatter: %s\n' "$m" "$f" "${err//$'\n'/ }"
        return 1
    fi
    err="$(ajv validate "${AJV[@]}" --all-errors --errors=json -s "$schema" -d "$json" 2>&1 >/dev/null)" && return 0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$m" "$f" "$line"
    done < <(tail -n +2 <<<"$err" | yq -p json '.[] | (.instancePath + " " + .message) | sub("^ "; "")' 2>/dev/null ||
        tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$err" | sed 's/ *$/\n/')
    return 1
}

# the dir a module is found in
_dir() { skogai module show "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' 'NR == 1 && NF == 2 { print $2; f = 1 } END { exit !f }'; }

# every module that requires type
_typed() {
    local m dir
    while read -r m _; do

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# what every module that requires type is held to, run by `skogai module test`
# with SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE set: each schema/<x>.json compiles, has a glob, and
# ships tests/fixtures/<x>/valid/* that pass and tests/fixtures/<x>/invalid/*

schemas() { compgen -G "$(module_dir)/schema/*.json" || true; }

@test "type contract: every schema/*.json compiles" {
    local s
    while IFS= read -r s; do
        [[ -n $s ]] || continue
        run ajv compile --spec=draft2020 --strict=true -s "$s"
        assert_status 0
    done < <(schemas)
}

@test "type contract: every schema has a glob in config" {
    local s
    while IFS= read -r s; do
        [[ -n $s ]] || continue
        run skogai config get "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE.schema.$(basename "$s" .json)"
        assert_status 0
        [[ -n $output ]]
    done < <(schemas)
}

@test "type contract: every schema has valid and invalid fixtures" {
    local s x d
    while IFS= read -r s; do
        [[ -n $s ]] || continue
        x="$(basename "$s" .json)"
        for d in valid invalid; do
            compgen -G "$(module_dir)/tests/fixtures/$x/$d/*" >/dev/null ||
                { echo "no fixtures: tests/fixtures/$x/$d/*" >&2; return 1; }
        done
    done < <(schemas)
}

@test "type contract: valid fixtures pass, each invalid one fails" {
    local s x f
    while IFS= read -r s; do
        [[ -n $s ]] || continue
        x="$(basename "$s" .json)"
        mapfile -t valid < <(compgen -G "$(module_dir)/tests/fixtures/$x/valid/*")
        run skogai type check --schema "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE.$x" "${valid[@]}"
        assert_status 0
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            run skogai type check --schema "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE.$x" "$f"
            assert_status 1
            assert_output_has "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE	$f	"
        done < <(compgen -G "$(module_dir)/tests/fixtures/$x/invalid/*")
    done < <(schemas)
}

@test "type contract: type check passes in a fresh repo" {
    run skogai type check "$SKOGAI_TEST_MODULE"
    assert_status 0
}

Status: draft, 2026-10-14. The first pieces exist in `projects/claude-code`.
Open work is tracked in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

## Goal

skogai is the orchestration layer. The main session discusses things with
skogix and decides. It uses tools and other agents to do the bulk of the
work: implementing, researching, reading and summarizing.

## Scope of this folder

`projects/orchestration/` holds only what has been discussed and is
active. `wip/` is temporary and still being tested. Something moves from
`wip/` into here only after we discuss it and adopt it.

## Big picture

`projects/claude-code` is the collection of Claude Code setups, and also
the test bed for orchestration. The orchestrator is the agent that does
what we have been doing by hand: it spawns other setups.

| Orchestration idea | What it is in `projects/claude-code` |
|---|---|
| Worker kind or role | A setup, e.g. `commit-msg`, later `reviewer` or `implementer` |
| Handoff contract v0 | `bin/agent`: prompt in on stdin, one message out on stdout |
| Proof that a worker is good | Its cases and evals. A setup is tested before it is relied on |
| The orchestrator | A setup too (`orchestration`). Its main tool is "run setup X with this prompt" |
| `TOOLS.md` | Mostly the list of setups: what each one is for and when to use it |

# claude-code test environment

Start from a Claude Code agent with everything stripped, then add one feature at a time and prove it with a test.

Each run happens in a throwaway sandbox at `/tmp/claude-code/$SETUP/`:

- `config/` is `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: transcripts (`projects/*/*.jsonl`), `.claude.json`, settings, and any other state the run creates. `.credentials.json` is a symlink to `~/.claude`.
- `work/` is the working directory.

The sandbox is wiped at the start of every run (`KEEP=1` reuses it), so what's in it afterwards came from that run only.

## Setups

A setup is `setups/<name>/` containing:

- `settings.json`: copied into the sandbox as its user settings.
- `system-prompt.md`: replaces the default system prompt.
- `append-system-prompt.md`: optional. Appended to the default system prompt (or to `system-prompt.md` if both exist).
- `work/`: optional. Copied into the working dir (for CLAUDE.md, `.claude/`, fixtures).

## Commands

- `bin/agent`: a one-shot agent. The prompt comes on stdin. Env vars: `SETUP` (baseline), `MODEL` (haiku), `TOOLS` (none), `OUTPUT` (text), `KEEP`. Extra args are passed to `claude`.
- `bin/inspect`: prints the session surface and the context size of a trivial turn.
- `bin/transcript`: prints the path of the latest transcript in the sandbox.
- `bin/eval <setup>`: runs `cases/<setup>/*` and saves results to `runs/<setup>/<stamp>/`.
- `bin/review <setup>`: prints every response in the latest run. `bin/compare <setup>` diffs the last two runs.
- `tests/run`: runs `tests/NN-*.sh`.

See CLAUDE.md for workflows and gotchas.

# dash-skogai types

one section per type, in [type/index.md](type/index.md) order. each type says which files every instance of it **owns** (creates and manages, exactly one owner), **writes** (modifies without owning) and **watches** (reads, wants to know about changes). `<name>` in a path is the instance's name.

## type

a kind of thing, and the files each of its instances owns, writes and watches.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  t(["type"])
  t -->|owns| p0["type/#lt;name#gt;.md"]
  t -->|owns| p1["type/#lt;name#gt;.schema.json"]
```

- **fields:** `type`, `title`, `description`, `fields`, `owns`, `writes`, `watches`
- **owns:** `type/<name>.md`, `type/<name>.schema.json`

a type defines a kind of thing. its definition is `type/<name>.md`, its instances live in `type/<name>/`, and `type/<name>.schema.json`, when there is one, is the schema for those instances. so [type.schema.json](type/type.schema.json) is the schema for every type definition.

### base

every instance of every type has the okf base. okf requires only `type`; the rest is optional:

- **identity**: `type`, `title`, `description`.
- **provenance**: `sources[]`, `usage_window`.
- **trust**: `generated: {by, at}`, `verified[]`.
- **lifecycle**: `status`, `stale_after`.

# skogix mobile — handover

tl;dr: Samsung Note 9 with a broken screen. All files, contacts, SMS, call log and app installers are backed up. adb is authorized, the lock screen is gone, and Claude can see and tap the phone through adb, so the broken screen no longer blocks anything. Remaining work: app data (chat apps), moving the backup off this machine, and optional extra ways in.

## device

- Samsung Galaxy Note 9, `SM-N960F`, Android 10, adb serial `299365e4f11c7ece`
- screen: broken. The display is readable, but touch only works near the bottom.
- USB IDs: `04e8:6860` = file transfer (+adb), `04e8:6863` = USB tethering (no file access)
- 466G storage, about 75G used; `/sdcard` is about 17G

## state of the phone (set 2026-10-29/30)

- Developer options: on (for years). USB debugging: on.
- this computer is authorized for adb. On Android 10 that authorization doesn't expire.
- lock screen: credential cleared (`locksettings clear`) and disabled (`locksettings set-disabled true`)
  - the old lock pattern was set 13 March. Fingerprints were most likely wiped when it was cleared.
- stay awake while charging: `stay_on_while_plugged_in=7`
- Default USB configuration: "Transferring files / Android Auto"

## backups (on this machine — not yet copied anywhere else)

| path | contents |
|------|----------|
| `~/phone-backup/` | `adb pull -a /sdcard/` — 51,509 files, 17G, 0 skipped |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/apks/` | 191 of 192 user-app APKs, 9.3G (missing: `com.geewa.smashingfour`, reinstall from the Play Store) |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/contacts.txt` | raw `content query` dump of `content://com.android.contacts/data` |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/sms.txt` | all SMS — **sensitive**, includes verification codes |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/calls.txt` | call log |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/packages-*.txt` | installed packages: user-installed only, and all |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/settings-*.txt` | `settings list` for global, secure and system |
| `~/phone-backup-meta/adbkey{,.pub}` | copy of `~/.android/adbkey` — **sensitive**: any machine with this key is trusted by the phone |

The contacts, SMS and call log are raw dumps, not files a new phone can import.

`~/phone-backup-meta/verify/` was not created by Claude.

## reconnect

```
lsusb | grep 04e8          # should show 6860 (not 6863 = tethering)
adb devices                # should list 299365e4f11c7ece  device
scrcpy                     # phone screen on the desktop, mouse/keyboard control
```

- `scrcpy` prints VA-API errors on this machine. They only mean video is decoded in software instead of on the GPU; it still works.
- if the phone is missing from `lsusb` entirely, it's the cable or port, not a phone setting.

## controlling the phone without touch (what Claude uses)

```
adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png                       # screenshot (1440x2960)
adb shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/ui.xml && adb shell cat /sdcard/ui.xml   # find element bounds
adb shell input tap X Y
adb shell input swipe 720 2300 720 900 300                   # scroll down
adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_BACK
adb shell am start -a android.settings.APPLICATION_DEVELOPMENT_SETTINGS
```

## open items

- [ ] app data: WhatsApp, Signal and other chat apps need their own in-app backups. Android 10 doesn't let adb read app data. Run them through scrcpy.
- [ ] move `~/phone-backup*` off this machine, especially `sms.txt` and `adbkey`
- [ ] delete the leftover `/sdcard/ui.xml` (Claude created it while reading screens): `adb shell rm /sdcard/ui.xml`
- [ ] optional: adb over Wi-Fi (`adb tcpip 5555` then `adb connect <ip>:5555`) — resets on reboot, and anyone on the same network can connect while it's on
- [ ] optional: Samsung Find My Mobile → Remote unlock, for a way in that doesn't depend on this computer
- [ ] optional: USB-C hub with an OTG mouse and HDMI (DeX), for using the phone with no computer at all
- [ ] decide whether to set a lock screen again (currently none)

tool_response.stdout:
Print email threads and calendar changes as they happen: piped or with --json, one
JSON object per line; at a terminal, one text line each. Runs until interrupted. What
changed before the watch began is not reported, unless --since reads back to it first —
save a change from just before it: HEY's clock is read to the whole second, and taken back
by however long reading it took, so a change up to a second before the watch asked, plus
that request's time, may be reported. Its "at" says when it happened.

Changes can drive a command instead of being printed, and that is a choice between two
behaviours: --run-async spawns the command per change and moves on, so a slow one never
holds up the watch and two can overlap; --run-sync waits for each and runs them in order.
Pass one or the other.

Every added and updated line says whether the thread is new mail: unseen, not muted, and
active since the watch last saw it — or since the watch began, for a thread it has not
seen, so the backlog --since reads is not new. Reading a thread, muting or
moving it is not new activity; a reply on a known thread is. --events new selects the new
ones, alone or alongside added, updated and deleted, and a script sees HEY_NEW=1 for them.

The calendars are followed too, by default: recording_added, recording_updated and
recording_deleted cover every recording the calendars hold — events, todos, habits and
their completions, journal entries, time tracks, countdowns and day titles — each line
naming its calendar; calendar_added, calendar_updated and calendar_deleted are
the calendars themselves coming and going. The email-specific flags switch the calendars
off: --box scopes the watch to mail, and an --events list naming only mail changes
(added, updated, deleted, new, resync) does the same.

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in AGENTS.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Currently working on: nothing; F002 (direct delegation) and F003 (plan-first delegation) of .skogai/skills/herdr-orchestration/ passing 2026-11-06
- Next up: skogix names the next feature; open gaps: plan rejection path and claude plan-mode status/shift+tab order never observed live

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + mise (tasks/tools) + jq/yq + argc; tests in bats; no tests and no coverage measurement yet
- Architecture: orchestration layer — the main interface where skogix and Claude plan and delegate; holds agents/skills (`.skogai/`, symlinked into `.claude/`), config, and `dash-skogai/`
- Priority order for machine health: mise dotfiles, then bootstrap, then doctor ("no dotfiles, no backup and no future")
- Delegation rule: checks only detect. A finding with `outside_repo: true` is never acted on directly by an agent; it becomes its own features.json feature that skogix approves

## Domain: herdr

### Decisions
- Oversight and messaging use existing herdr commands only, documented in dash-skogai/type/tool/herdr.md; no scripts (skogix: the removed orchestrate skill wrote its own tools instead of using what exists) (2026-11-06)
- Messaging goes through herdr (`agent prompt` default, `pane send-text` + `send-keys enter` tmux-style), not Claude Code's SendMessage (skogix 2026-11-06)
- Orchestration follows the vv-harness plugin skill /vv-harness:harness-orchestrate (source skogai2/skogharness skills/harness-orchestrate/; the local .skogai/skills/herdr-orchestration copy was retired in PR #13, 2026-11-06); workers launch in auto mode (claude --permission-mode auto, codex --approve-for-me), never bypass flags (skogix 2026-11-06)
- The controller never answers trust prompts (codex folder trust, claude CLAUDE.md imports); notify skogix (2026-11-06)

### Gotchas
- Claude transcripts are under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects = /skogai/claude/projects, not ~/.claude/projects
- herdr's claude hook reports agent_session only on SessionStart; agents without one since show null
- a claude started under ~/skogai can block on the external CLAUDE.md imports dialog; after answering, plain `agent wait` returns at once on the stale blocked state. It is asked once per project: for ~/skogai WarningShown=true, Approved=false, so workers there now start without the dialog and without external imports
- `agent start` rejects multi-line argv (invalid_agent_argument); returns agent_pane_busy right after `tab create`; may return timeout while the tui is fine, then the agent name is unregistered (use pane id)
- a controller Claude Code in auto mode refuses to start a worker with --dangerously-skip-permissions ("Create Unsafe Agents")
- unfocused codex workers settle `idle`, claude `done`: wait with --until done --until idle (seen twice: F002, F003)
- a plan-first claude worker can reach its plan menu before herdr sees it ready: agent start returns agent_not_ready; read the screen. Full plan is in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/plans/<slug>.md; menu option 'Yes, and use auto mode' keeps it unattended (F003)
- the vv-harness plugin agent types can drop out mid-session; the spec gate then runs as a general-purpose agent given /skogai/claude/plugins/cache/skogix/vv-harness/<ver>/agents/spec-verification.md (F003)

## Domain: lint (hk)

### Gotchas
- hk fix-mode hooks (pre-commit) apply a step's `check_diff` patch; overriding only `check`/`fix` in hk.pkl leaves the builtin check_diff (for shfmt: tabs) in charge of every commit. hk.pkl now overrides shfmt check_diff (2026-11-06)
- one shellcheck error (SC1128) can mask warnings in the same batch; re-run after fixing

## Domain: Machine checks

### Decisions
- bash/mise/jq chosen: matches existing tooling in the repo, no build step (2026-10-29)
- Check = `bin/checks/<name>`, read-only, findings JSON array in `.skogai/logs/findings/<name>.json` (gitignored); finding fields: id, check, observed, expected, suggested_fix, outside_repo; no file contents or env values in findings (2026-10-29)
- init.sh targets: smoke (`bash -n` + `jq empty` on tracked files), full_test (smoke + `bats -r tests/unit`, fixture-driven via fake `mise` on PATH), machine_check (`bats -r tests/machine`, live, never in full_test), focused_test (one .bats) (2026-10-29)
- A feature passes on its tests/unit fixtures; a red tests/machine run is a finding to delegate, not a broken feature (2026-10-29)
- No doctor baseline/ratchet: `mise doctor` reported 0 errors after cleanup (2026-10-29)
- Remote stays HTTPS (`https://github.com/skogai2/skogai.git`); skogix declined switching to SSH (2026-10-29)

### Patterns
- Compare TOML semantically (python tomllib walk) against a known-good checkpoint from `~/.local/state/mise/history/repo.git` instead of reading text diffs

### Gotchas
- 2026-10-29 incident: an unknown writer rewrote ~/.config/mise/config.toml at 12:41 (checkpoint 787) — nested arrays/inline tables became strings, quoted-key `[bootstrap.*]` tables were dropped. Re-adding dotfiles entries without their include/exclude let the next sync publish secrets to skogai2/.dotfiles. Filters restored (checkpoint 825), secrets rotated by skogix; the leaked (now dead) values stay in origin history — purge skipped
- `mise dot status` warns `invalid file entry` and silently drops the entry from tracking; F002 turns that into a finding
- `~/.local/bin/mise` (2026.10.17) shadows the pacman `/usr/bin/mise` (2026.10.21)
- verify-git-identity.sh checks SSH identity, but pushes go over HTTPS — the credential helper decides the actual pushing account
- `trap '... $local_var' EXIT` inside a function fails under `set -u` once the function has returned; expand the value when setting the trap
- Commands run with Claude Code's `!` prefix are not recorded in atuin: the 2026-10-29 21:18 convergence run that succeeded is missing there, so atuin alone made the chain look always-failing
- commit-gate hook rejects `git add` and `git commit` in one Bash call; when a rejected call also held the add, the next commit silently picks up only the earlier-staged files. Check `git show --stat` after any hook rejection

## Domain: auto mode

### Gotchas
- `rtk hook claude` (PreToolUse Bash, user settings /skogai/claude/settings.json) rewrites commands (cat→rtk read, grep→rtk grep). Auto mode then returns "no verdict, a hook changed the input" and allows one identical retry. Calls matched by an allow rule (`git *`) went through. `rtk hook claude` has no flag to skip the rewrite (2026-11-06)

## Improve-Harness Result: read-only Bash under auto mode (2026-11-06)
- Outcome: pending (rerun not done yet)
- Proof: baseline: in session 5bf125a1, all 4 rewritten Bash calls without an allow rule got "no verdict"; the `git add`/`git commit` calls (allowed by `Bash(git *)`) passed
- Hypothesis: if read-only rtk subcommands (diff, grep, json, ls, read, recall, rg, tree, wc) are allowlisted in .claude/settings.json, then a fresh session's `cat`/`grep`/`ls` calls run without the classifier error, because the allow rule matches the rewritten command. Weakened if the error still appears, meaning rules match the command before the rewrite. `rtk find` is left out because find can `-exec`/`-delete`
- Relay/latency: hypothesis and change in the same session; a fresh-session rerun is still needed
- Risk vs. carrying cost: 9 allow rules; they bypass auto-mode review only for rtk's read-only proxies
- Decision: retain if the fresh session shows no "no verdict" error on a plain `cat`/`grep`; remove the rules if the error persists
- Known limits: covers only Bash reads in this repo, on CLI 2.1.318 with rtk's current rewrite table

# Context Summary

Persistent record of architectural decisions, discovered patterns, gotchas, and active context.
This file is referenced in AGENTS.md and loaded every session.

## Active Context
- Currently working on: nothing; F002 (direct delegation) and F003 (plan-first delegation) of .skogai/skills/herdr-orchestration/ passing 2026-11-06
- Next up: skogix names the next feature; open gaps: plan rejection path and claude plan-mode status/shift+tab order never observed live

## Cross-Cutting Concerns
- Stack: bash + mise (tasks/tools) + jq/yq + argc; tests in bats; no tests and no coverage measurement yet
- Architecture: orchestration layer — the main interface where skogix and Claude plan and delegate; holds agents/skills (`.skogai/`, symlinked into `.claude/`), config, and `dash-skogai/`
- Priority order for machine health: mise dotfiles, then bootstrap, then doctor ("no dotfiles, no backup and no future")
- Delegation rule: checks only detect. A finding with `outside_repo: true` is never acted on directly by an agent; it becomes its own features.json feature that skogix approves

## Domain: herdr

### Decisions
- Oversight and messaging use existing herdr commands only, documented in dash-skogai/type/tool/herdr.md; no scripts (skogix: the removed orchestrate skill wrote its own tools instead of using what exists) (2026-11-06)
- Messaging goes through herdr (`agent prompt` default, `pane send-text` + `send-keys enter` tmux-style), not Claude Code's SendMessage (skogix 2026-11-06)
- Orchestration follows the vv-harness plugin skill /vv-harness:harness-orchestrate (source skogai2/skogharness skills/harness-orchestrate/; the local .skogai/skills/herdr-orchestration copy was retired in PR #13, 2026-11-06); workers launch in auto mode (claude --permission-mode auto, codex --approve-for-me), never bypass flags (skogix 2026-11-06)
- The controller never answers trust prompts (codex folder trust, claude CLAUDE.md imports); notify skogix (2026-11-06)

### Gotchas
- Claude transcripts are under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects = /skogai/claude/projects, not ~/.claude/projects
- herdr's claude hook reports agent_session only on SessionStart; agents without one since show null
- a claude started under ~/skogai can block on the external CLAUDE.md imports dialog; after answering, plain `agent wait` returns at once on the stale blocked state. It is asked once per project: for ~/skogai WarningShown=true, Approved=false, so workers there now start without the dialog and without external imports
- `agent start` rejects multi-line argv (invalid_agent_argument); returns agent_pane_busy right after `tab create`; may return timeout while the tui is fine, then the agent name is unregistered (use pane id)
- a controller Claude Code in auto mode refuses to start a worker with --dangerously-skip-permissions ("Create Unsafe Agents")
- unfocused codex workers settle `idle`, claude `done`: wait with --until done --until idle (seen twice: F002, F003)
- a plan-first claude worker can reach its plan menu before herdr sees it ready: agent start returns agent_not_ready; read the screen. Full plan is in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/plans/<slug>.md; menu option 'Yes, and use auto mode' keeps it unattended (F003)
- the vv-harness plugin agent types can drop out mid-session; the spec gate then runs as a general-purpose agent given /skogai/claude/plugins/cache/skogix/vv-harness/<ver>/agents/spec-verification.md (F003)

## Domain: lint (hk)

### Gotchas
- hk fix-mode hooks (pre-commit) apply a step's `check_diff` patch; overriding only `check`/`fix` in hk.pkl leaves the builtin check_diff (for shfmt: tabs) in charge of every commit. hk.pkl now overrides shfmt check_diff (2026-11-06)
- one shellcheck error (SC1128) can mask warnings in the same batch; re-run after fixing

## Domain: Machine checks

### Decisions
- bash/mise/jq chosen: matches existing tooling in the repo, no build step (2026-10-29)
- Check = `bin/checks/<name>`, read-only, findings JSON array in `.skogai/logs/findings/<name>.json` (gitignored); finding fields: id, check, observed, expected, suggested_fix, outside_repo; no file contents or env values in findings (2026-10-29)
- init.sh targets: smoke (`bash -n` + `jq empty` on tracked files), full_test (smoke + `bats -r tests/unit`, fixture-driven via fake `mise` on PATH), machine_check (`bats -r tests/machine`, live, never in full_test), focused_test (one .bats) (2026-10-29)
- A feature passes on its tests/unit fixtures; a red tests/machine run is a finding to delegate, not a broken feature (2026-10-29)
- No doctor baseline/ratchet: `mise doctor` reported 0 errors after cleanup (2026-10-29)
- Remote stays HTTPS (`https://github.com/skogai2/skogai.git`); skogix declined switching to SSH (2026-10-29)
- bin/checks/, tests/machine/ and the machine_check target were removed with the harness on 2026-10-31 (a2bd3bf) and not restored at re-init; the decisions above are history (2026-11-05)
- `.claude/settings.json` = harness stamp merged with skogix's prior settings (hooks concatenated, permissions unioned, `defaultMode: auto` kept); harness statusLine replaced `wt list statusline` (2026-10-29); same merge redone at re-init, statusLine again the harness one by skogix's choice (2026-11-05)

### Patterns
- Compare TOML semantically (python tomllib walk) against a known-good checkpoint from `~/.local/state/mise/history/repo.git` instead of reading text diffs

### Gotchas
- 2026-10-29 incident: an unknown writer rewrote ~/.config/mise/config.toml at 12:41 (checkpoint 787) — nested arrays/inline tables became strings, quoted-key `[bootstrap.*]` tables were dropped. Re-adding dotfiles entries without their include/exclude let the next sync publish secrets to skogai2/.dotfiles. Filters restored (checkpoint 825), secrets rotated by skogix; the leaked (now dead) values stay in origin history — purge skipped
- `mise dot status` warns `invalid file entry` and silently drops the entry from tracking; F002 turns that into a finding
- `~/.local/bin/mise` (2026.10.17) shadows the pacman `/usr/bin/mise` (2026.10.21)
- verify-git-identity.sh checks SSH identity, but pushes go over HTTPS — the credential helper decides the actual pushing account
- `trap '... $local_var' EXIT` inside a function fails under `set -u` once the function has returned; expand the value when setting the trap
- Commands run with Claude Code's `!` prefix are not recorded in atuin: the 2026-10-29 21:18 convergence run that succeeded is missing there, so atuin alone made the chain look always-failing
- commit-gate hook rejects `git add` and `git commit` in one Bash call; when a rejected call also held the add, the next commit silently picks up only the earlier-staged files. Check `git show --stat` after any hook rejection

## Domain: auto mode

### Gotchas
- `rtk hook claude` (PreToolUse Bash, user settings /skogai/claude/settings.json) rewrites commands (cat→rtk read, grep→rtk grep). Auto mode then returns "no verdict, a hook changed the input" and allows one identical retry. Calls matched by an allow rule (`git *`) went through. `rtk hook claude` has no flag to skip the rewrite (2026-11-06)

## Improve-Harness Result: read-only Bash under auto mode (2026-11-06)
- Outcome: pending (rerun not done yet)
- Proof: baseline: in session 5bf125a1, all 4 rewritten Bash calls without an allow rule got "no verdict"; the `git add`/`git commit` calls (allowed by `Bash(git *)`) passed
- Hypothesis: if read-only rtk subcommands (diff, grep, json, ls, read, recall, rg, tree, wc) are allowlisted in .claude/settings.json, then a fresh session's `cat`/`grep`/`ls` calls run without the classifier error, because the allow rule matches the rewritten command. Weakened if the error still appears, meaning rules match the command before the rewrite. `rtk find` is left out because find can `-exec`/`-delete`
- Relay/latency: hypothesis and change in the same session; a fresh-session rerun is still needed
- Risk vs. carrying cost: 9 allow rules; they bypass auto-mode review only for rtk's read-only proxies
- Decision: retain if the fresh session shows no "no verdict" error on a plain `cat`/`grep`; remove the rules if the error persists

## Meta-Patterns
<!-- Coordination insights that apply across features — NOT domain-specific.
     Populated by the retrospective step at session end.

# skogai

how an agent runs [skogai](../type/tool/skogai.md) until the cli has the command. only `config` exists so far, as `argc config` ([skogai-config](../bin/skogai-config.md)). each section is one command, written as a prompt: hand an agent this file and the command name.

paths are relative to the dash root, the folder holding `type/`. `<dot>` is the dot to check. in this repo it is `src`, later `./.skogai`.

## check

pure. reports type errors, writes nothing. safe to run unattended.

do not edit, create or delete any file. if something looks fixable, report it; do not fix it.

run each command exactly as written, one per shell call, from the dash root: no `cd`, `&&`, `;` or pipes. an unattended run allows only these commands, so a chained one is denied.

1. **ref**: run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain type/`. report the commit, and `dirty` if `type/` has uncommitted changes.
2. **okn**: run `okn validate <dot>`. every okn error is a check error.
3. **cases**: read every `type/<name>.md`. a file whose frontmatter has `type: type` is a case: its `title` is the tag, with its `fields` and `owns`. a file without that frontmatter is a stub: report it as a warning, not a case.
4. **files**: list every file in `<dot>` with `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard <dot>`.
5. **owners**: for each file, find the cases whose `owns` patterns match its path relative to `<dot>`. `<name>` matches one path segment, and a pattern ending in `/` matches everything under it.
   - no owner: `untyped`.
   - two or more owners: `conflict`, naming the owners.
6. **tags**: for each `.md` file, read its frontmatter.
   - no `type`: `untagged`.
   - a `type` that is not a case: `unknown tag`.
   - a field from the case's `fields` missing: `missing field`.
7. **derived**: skip. how a type declares a derived file is still open (see [TODO](../TODO.md)). say it was skipped.

### output

one line per finding, then a summary:

```text
error   <path>: untyped
error   <path>: unknown tag "index"
warning type/task.md: stub, no frontmatter
skipped derived files: not specified
dash    <commit> [dirty]
result  errors=<n> warnings=<n>
```

`result errors=0` is clean. do not add advice after the summary.

## plan

not written yet. depends on where a dot records its dash ref and how layers merge (see [TODO](../TODO.md)).

## apply

not written yet. the only writer: needs human approval, never automated.

file.content:
---
type: type
title: type
description: a kind of thing, and the files each of its instances owns, writes and watches.
fields: [type, title, description, fields, owns, writes, watches]
owns: [type/<name>.md, type/<name>.schema.json]
---

# type

a type defines a kind of thing. its definition is `type/<name>.md`, its instances live in `type/<name>/`, and `type/<name>.schema.json`, when there is one, is the schema for those instances. so [type.schema.json](type.schema.json) is the schema for every type definition.

## base

every instance of every type has the okf base. okf requires only `type`; the rest is optional:

- **identity**: `type`, `title`, `description`.
- **provenance**: `sources[]`, `usage_window`.
- **trust**: `generated: {by, at}`, `verified[]`.
- **lifecycle**: `status`, `stale_after`.

## definition

every type states:

- **type**: `type`.
- **title**: its name. instances carry it as their `type` in frontmatter.
- **fields**: the frontmatter every instance must have, beyond `type`.
- **owns**: the paths each instance creates and manages fully. every path has exactly one owner.
- **writes**: the paths each instance modifies without owning them.

---
type: type
title: tool
description: an executable skogai uses, with its wrapper, scripts and workflow.
fields: [type, title]
owns: [type/tool/<name>.md, bin/<name>, scripts/<name>/, workflows/<name>.md]
---

# tool

instances: [herdr](tool/herdr.md), [wt](tool/wt.md), [gita](tool/gita.md), [mise](tool/mise.md), [okn](tool/okn.md), [skogai](tool/skogai.md).

a tool `<name>` owns:

- `type/tool/<name>.md`: the instance, and its documentation.
- `bin/<name>`: the entrypoint.
- `scripts/<name>/`: everything the entrypoint calls.
- `workflows/<name>.md`: how and when to use it.

---
type: type
title: router
description: a file that points to other files, so an agent loads only what the task needs.
status: draft
fields: [type, title]
owns: [<name>/SKOGAI.md, <name>/CLAUDE.md]
---

# router

a router routes, it does not hold content. its body is one `<routes>` block: the frontmatter `type` names the block, as `router` names `<routes>`.

```markdown
---
type: router
title: dash-skogai
---

<routes>

- @type/index.md - small index, loaded with the router
- tmp/ - untyped or undecided, read when needed

</routes>
```

- **entries**: one per line, `- <path> [- <description>]`. the description lets an agent decide without opening the file.
- **`@path`**: loaded with the router. use it for small routers and indexes.
- **plain path**: listed, read on demand. use it for anything with real content.

---
type: type
title: rule
description: a constraint that can be checked, enforcing a decision.
fields: [type, title, applies_to]
owns: [type/rule/<name>.md]
watches: [<applies_to>]
---

# rule

a rule is a decision made checkable.

- **applies_to**: the paths the rule constrains. the rule watches them and is re-checked when they change.
- **from**: optional, the decision it enforces.

a "we do X" that cannot be checked is a decision, not a rule.

---
type: type
title: decision
description: a choice and why it was made, written once.
fields: [type, title, status]
owns: [type/decision/<nnnn>-<name>.md]
writes: [DECISIONS.md]
---

# decision

a decision records a choice and why. it is written once and never edited.

- **status**: `proposed`, `accepted` or `superseded`.
- **supersedes**: optional, the number of the decision this one replaces.

to change a decision, write a new one that supersedes it. `DECISIONS.md` is derived from the instances and never edited by hand.

---
type: type
title: trigger
description: a script that runs when a file changes or an event happens.
fields: [type, title, when]
owns: [type/trigger/<name>.md, scripts/trigger/<name>.sh]
watches: [<when>]
---

# trigger

a trigger `<name>` owns:

- `type/trigger/<name>.md`: the instance.
- `scripts/trigger/<name>.sh`: what runs.

- **when**: the paths or events that run the script.

the base `watches` field is the simplest trigger: it marks interest in a path and runs nothing. a trigger adds the script.

---
type: type
title: event
description: something that happened, recorded as one row appended to the event log.
fields: [type, title]
owns: [type/event/<name>.md, type/event/<name>.schema.json, scripts/event/<name>.sh]
writes: [.skogai/logs/event.jsonl]
---

# event

an event is something that happened, such as a turn ending or a tool about to run. each time it happens, one row is appended to the event log. rows are never edited; the log as a whole is temporary and can be deleted.

an event `<name>` owns:

- `type/event/<name>.md`: the instance. it says what happened and when it fires.
- `type/event/<name>.schema.json`: its rows. it narrows the row in [event.schema.json](event.schema.json) to this event's `input`.
- `scripts/event/<name>.sh`: what runs when it happens.

- **enabled**: optional. an event runs only when this is `true`. missing, or no instance at all, is off.

## the row

one json object per line in `.skogai/logs/event.jsonl`:

- **ts**: when it happened, utc, to the millisecond.
- **event**: the instance's `title`.
- **action**: optional, what the script did, when it did more than record the row.
- **input**: everything the event came with, unchanged. `$defs/input` in the schema lists the fields every event shares; `type/event/<name>.schema.json` adds its own and says which are required.

# routes 

- @src/index.md [@TODO]
- @type/index.md [@TODO]

# layout

- `./`: the meta top-layer, here we are creating for someone how we work on dash (CLAUDE.md, SKOGAI.md, TODO.md)
- `type/`: one file per type, each acting as a module
- `src/`: the future dot, an okn bundle. check with `okn validate src`
- `Argcfile.sh`, `bin/`: the cli, run as `argc <cmd>`. see [skogai-config](bin/skogai-config.md)
- `system/`, `global/`, `local/`, `mise.config.toml`: config layers for `argc config`
- `tmp/`: untyped or undecided. `tmp/docs/` holds argc docs

# design goals

skogai is functional: idempotent, immutable and strictly typed.

- **closed union**: a dot is a discriminated union of skogai types. okf `type` is the tag, dash defines the cases, and an unknown tag or untagged file is a type error.
- **layers, not inheritance**: the resolved state is `fold(merge, [base, global, local])`, later layer wins. no layer knows about the others.
- **git is the immutability model**: content is immutable, a change is a patch, history is the append-only log. types do not declare mutability.
- **refs resolve to commits**: a dot names dash by ref. every result reports the commit it resolved to, so it can be reproduced.
- **generated where possible**: a file derived from others (e.g. `DECISIONS.md`) is never hand-edited, and `check` regenerates and compares it.
- **pure by default**: only `apply` writes. see [skogai](type/tool/skogai.md).
- **don't rebuild okn**: list, validate, search and the rest belong to [okn](type/tool/okn.md).

# handover

## how to work here

- listen to what skogix says. he is probably saying it for a reason.
- one thing at a time. when proposals, plans, extra steps and questions should be added to TODO.md to be managed with the focus and attention they deserve.
- understand what the intent, goal and actual changes needed are before running anything.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* variables are injected by argc at runtime
set -e

# @cmd skogai-config
# @arg args~[?`_choice_script`]
config() { _run_script "$@"; }

_run_script() {
  bash "./bin/skogai-${FUNCNAME[1]}" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* variables are injected by argc at runtime
# @describe read and write key/value config across system, global and local layers
# @meta require-tools git,yq
# @meta binname config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_SYSTEM_DIR=system  dir of the system layer config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_SYSTEM_FILE=mise.config.toml name of the system config file
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_GLOBAL_DIR=global  dir of the global layer config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_GLOBAL_FILE=mise.config.toml name of the global file
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_LOCAL_DIR=local  dir of the local layer config
# @env SKOGAI_CONFIG_LOCAL_FILE=mise.config.toml name of the local config file
set -euo pipefail

# joins the items of a list value; `get` prints one item per line
SEP=$'\x1f'

# layers in fold order, later wins: system, global, local
_layer_file() {
  local dir="SKOGAI_CONFIG_${1^^}_DIR" file="SKOGAI_CONFIG_${1^^}_FILE"
  echo "${!dir}/${!file}"
}

# x.md -> x.local.md
_local_md() { echo "${1%.md}.local.md"; }

# --file layers in fold order: each x.md, then its x.local.md
_file_layers() {
  local f
  for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do
    echo "$f"
    _local_md "$f"
  done
}

# `.` is a relation, `-` is part of a name: stage.on-stop -> SKOGAI_STAGE_ONSTOP
_env_name() {
  local k="${1^^}"
  k="${k//-/}"
  echo "SKOGAI_${k//./_}"
}

# a frontmatter file as "key<TAB>tag<TAB>value" lines: nested maps flatten to
# dotted keys, under --scope if given, with `_` read as `-`. a list is one
# value, its items joined by SEP.
_frontmatter() {
  SEP="$SEP" SCOPE="${argc_scope:-}" yq --front-matter=extract '
        select(document_index == 0) | select(tag == "!!map") | .. |
        select(tag == "!!seq" or (tag != "!!map" and (parent | tag) != "!!seq")) |
        [ ((strenv(SCOPE) | select(. != "") | [.]) // []) + path | join(".") | downcase | sub("_"; "-"),
          tag,
          (select(tag == "!!seq") | map(tostring) | join(strenv(SEP))) // tostring
        ] | join("\t")' "$1"
}

# prints "key<TAB>value<TAB>origin" for every resolved key
_resolve() {
  local -A val origin
  local layer file key value env tag
  for layer in system global local; do
    file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
    [[ -f $file ]] || continue
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
      key="${entry%%$'\n'*}"
      value="${entry#*$'\n'}"
      [[ $entry == *$'\n'* ]] || value=""
      val[$key]="$value"
      origin[$key]="$layer"
    done < <(git config -f "$file" --list -z)
  done
  local fm
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    [[ -f $file ]] || continue
    fm="$(_frontmatter "$file")" || exit 2
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r key tag value; do
      [[ -n $key ]] || continue
      if [[ $tag == '!!null' ]]; then
        builtin unset "val[$key]" "origin[$key]"
      else
        val[$key]="$value"
        origin[$key]="file:$file"
      fi
    done <<<"$fm"
  done < <(_file_layers)
  for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
    env="$(_env_name "$key")"
    if [[ -n ${!env+x} ]]; then
      val[$key]="${!env}"
      origin[$key]="env:$env"
    fi
  done
  for key in "${!val[@]}"; do
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${val[$key]}" "${origin[$key]}"
  done | sort
}

_target_file() {
  if [[ ${argc_global:-} == 1 ]]; then _layer_file global; else _layer_file local; fi
}

# every resolved key; choices for get and set, described by value when completing
_choice_key() {
  if [[ ${ARGC_COMPGEN:-0} == 1 ]]; then _resolve | cut -f1,2 | tr "$SEP" ' '; else _resolve | cut -f1; fi
}

# keys present in the layer set/unset write to; choices for unset
_choice_target_key() {
  local file
  if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
    if [[ -f $file ]]; then _frontmatter "$file" | cut -f1; fi
  else
    file="$(_target_file)"
    if [[ -f $file ]]; then git config -f "$file" --name-only --list; fi
  fi
}

# the frontmatter path of a key in a --file layer: the key minus --scope
_file_key() {
  local key="$1" scope="${argc_scope:-}"
  if [[ -n $scope ]]; then
    [[ $key == "$scope".* ]] || {
      echo "key $key is outside --scope $scope" >&2
      return 2
    }
    key="${key#"$scope".}"
  fi
  [[ $key =~ ^[^.]+(\.[^.]+)*$ ]] || {
    echo "bad key: $1" >&2
    return 2
  }
  echo "$key"
}

# @cmd print the resolved value of a key; a list prints one item per line
# @flag --show-origin  also print which layer the value came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
# @arg key![`_choice_key`]
get() {
  local line
  line="$(_resolve | awk -F'\t' -v k="$argc_key" '$1 == k')" || exit 2
  if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(cut -f3 <<<"$line")" "$(cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" ' ')"
  else
    cut -f2 <<<"$line" | tr "$SEP" '\n'
  fi
}

# @cmd set a key in the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  write to the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  write this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![?`_choice_key`]
# @arg value!
set() {
  local file key
  if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
    key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
    [[ -f $file ]] || printf -- '---\n{}\n---\n' >"$file"
    K="$key" V="$argc_value" \
      yq -i --front-matter=process 'setpath(strenv(K) | split("."); strenv(V) | from_yaml)' "$file"
    return
  fi
  file="$(_target_file)"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
  git config -f "$file" "$argc_key" "$argc_value"
}

# @cmd remove a key from the local layer, or the global one, or a --file's .local.md
# @flag --global  remove from the global layer instead of local
# @option --file  remove from this file's .local.md frontmatter instead
# @option --scope  the section --file keys are mounted under
# @arg key![`_choice_target_key`]
unset() {
  local file key
  if [[ -n ${argc_file:-} ]]; then
    key="$(_file_key "$argc_key")" || exit 2
    file="$(_local_md "$argc_file")"
    [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
    K="$key" \
      yq -i --front-matter=process 'delpaths([strenv(K) | split(".")])' "$file"
    return
  fi
  file="$(_target_file)"
  [[ -f $file ]] || exit 1
  git config -f "$file" --unset-all "$argc_key" || exit 1
}

# @cmd print every resolved key as key=value; a list prints one line per item
# @flag --show-origin  prefix each line with the layer it came from
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
list() {
  local key value origin item resolved
  resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
  [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
    while IFS= read -r -d "$SEP" item; do
      if [[ ${argc_show_origin:-} == 1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\t%s=%s\n' "$origin" "$key" "$item"
      else
        printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$item"
      fi
    done <<<"$value$SEP"
  done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the resolved config as export lines; a list's items are newline-separated
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  mount --file keys under this section
env() {
  local key value origin resolved
  resolved="$(_resolve)" || exit 2
  [[ -n $resolved ]] || return 0
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value origin; do
    printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$(_env_name "$key")" "${value//$SEP/$'\n'}"
  done <<<"$resolved"
}

# @cmd print the path of each layer file, and whether it exists
# @option --file*  a markdown file whose frontmatter is a layer, with its .local.md after it
# @option --scope  accepted for symmetry with get and list; unused
files() {
  local layer file
  for layer in system global local; do
    file="$(_layer_file "$layer")"
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$layer" "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
  done
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' file "$file" "$([[ -f $file ]] && echo present || echo missing)"
  done < <(_file_layers)
}

# type

a type defines a kind of thing. its definition is `type/<name>.md`, its instances live in `type/<name>/`, and `type/<name>.schema.json`, when there is one, is the schema for those instances. so [type.schema.json](type.schema.json) is the schema for every type definition.

## base

every instance of every type has the okf base. okf requires only `type`; the rest is optional:

- **identity**: `type`, `title`, `description`.
- **provenance**: `sources[]`, `usage_window`.
- **trust**: `generated: {by, at}`, `verified[]`.
- **lifecycle**: `status`, `stale_after`.

## definition

every type states:

- **type**: `type`.
- **title**: its name. instances carry it as their `type` in frontmatter.
- **fields**: the frontmatter every instance must have, beyond `type`.
- **owns**: the paths each instance creates and manages fully. every path has exactly one owner.
- **writes**: the paths each instance modifies without owning them.
- **watches**: the paths each instance reads and wants to know about when they change.

`<name>` in a path is the instance's name. a path ending in `/` is a folder.

## check

- a file with no owner is untyped: an error.
- a file with two owners is a conflict: an error.
- ownership is one step. `type` owns `type/tool.md`; `tool` owns `type/tool/gita.md`. `type` never owns what is under `type/tool/`.
- `writes` and `watches` can overlap freely.

`type` is itself a type: every `type/<name>.md` is an instance of it, including this file.
---
type: tool
title: skogai
---

# skogai

the cli that turns dash into a dot. it is a function over values: `check` and `plan` are pure, and `apply` is the only writer.

## values

- **dash**: type definitions and functions, named by ref and resolved to a commit at use.
- **layers**: `base` (dash@ref), `global` (`~/.skogai`), `local` (`<repo>/.skogai`). key/value settings use [skogai-config](../../bin/skogai-config.md).
- **resolved**: `fold(merge, [base, global, local])`, later layer wins.
- **dot**: the resolved value written to disk, a closed union of skogai types.

## commands

### `skogai config`

implemented in `bin/skogai-config`, run as `argc config`. see [skogai-config](../../bin/skogai-config.md).

### `skogai check [<dot>]`

pure. reports type errors, writes nothing.

1. runs `okn validate` on the dot.
2. every file has exactly one owner (see [type](../type.md#check)).
3. every `type` tag is a case dash defines, and the file has that case's `fields`.
4. every derived file equals its regeneration.

prints the dash ref and the commit it resolved to.

### `skogai resolve [<dot>]`

pure. prints the resolved value, and for each entry the layer it came from.

### `skogai plan [<dot>]`

pure. prints the patch `apply` would make, as a git diff. an empty patch means the dot is already up to date.

### `skogai apply [<dot>] [<patch>]`

the only writer. applies `<patch>`, or the output of `plan` if none is given, with `git apply`.

- idempotent: after `apply`, `plan` is empty.
- init is `apply` on an empty dot.
- moving to a newer dash is changing the ref, then `plan` and `apply`.

## conventions

- `<dot>` defaults to `./.skogai`.
- output goes to stdout, diagnostics to stderr.
- exit `0`: clean or empty patch. `1`: type errors or a non-empty patch. `2`: usage or internal error.
- `--json` on every command, for machine output.
- anything okn already does (list, search, view, validate) is called through okn, not rebuilt.

## open

see [TODO](../../TODO.md): where the dash ref is recorded, merge semantics per field, and how a type declares a derived file.

# router

a router routes, it does not hold content. its body is one `<routes>` block: the frontmatter `type` names the block, as `router` names `<routes>`.

```markdown
---
type: router
title: dash-skogai
---

<routes>

- @type/index.md - small index, loaded with the router
- tmp/ - untyped or undecided, read when needed

</routes>
```

- **entries**: one per line, `- <path> [- <description>]`. the description lets an agent decide without opening the file.
- **`@path`**: loaded with the router. use it for small routers and indexes.
- **plain path**: listed, read on demand. use it for anything with real content.
- **no transitive bloat**: a router never `@`-links a file that itself `@`-links content. that loads everything below it.
- **one step**: each router points to the next level, never to everything.

## CLAUDE.md

claude code loads only `CLAUDE.md`, never `SKOGAI.md`. so each router also owns the `CLAUDE.md` next to it, and that file is derived: its whole content is

```markdown
@SKOGAI.md
```

it is never hand-edited, and `check` regenerates and compares it. routes go in `SKOGAI.md`, not in `CLAUDE.md`.

the source this was folded from is [tmp/routing](../tmp/routing/README.md).
# skogai

how an agent runs [skogai](../type/tool/skogai.md) until the cli has the command. only `config` exists so far, as `argc config` ([skogai-config](../bin/skogai-config.md)). each section is one command, written as a prompt: hand an agent this file and the command name.

paths are relative to the dash root, the folder holding `type/`. `<dot>` is the dot to check. in this repo it is `src`, later `./.skogai`.

## check

pure. reports type errors, writes nothing. safe to run unattended.

do not edit, create or delete any file. if something looks fixable, report it; do not fix it.

run each command exactly as written, one per shell call, from the dash root: no `cd`, `&&`, `;` or pipes. an unattended run allows only these commands, so a chained one is denied.

1. **ref**: run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain type/`. report the commit, and `dirty` if `type/` has uncommitted changes.
2. **okn**: run `okn validate <dot>`. every okn error is a check error.
3. **cases**: read every `type/<name>.md`. a file whose frontmatter has `type: type` is a case: its `title` is the tag, with its `fields` and `owns`. a file without that frontmatter is a stub: report it as a warning, not a case.
4. **files**: list every file in `<dot>` with `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard <dot>`.
5. **owners**: for each file, find the cases whose `owns` patterns match its path relative to `<dot>`. `<name>` matches one path segment, and a pattern ending in `/` matches everything under it.
   - no owner: `untyped`.
   - two or more owners: `conflict`, naming the owners.
6. **tags**: for each `.md` file, read its frontmatter.
   - no `type`: `untagged`.
   - a `type` that is not a case: `unknown tag`.
   - a field from the case's `fields` missing: `missing field`.
7. **derived**: skip. how a type declares a derived file is still open (see [TODO](../TODO.md)). say it was skipped.

### output

one line per finding, then a summary:

```text
error   <path>: untyped
error   <path>: unknown tag "index"
warning type/task.md: stub, no frontmatter
skipped derived files: not specified
dash    <commit> [dirty]
result  errors=<n> warnings=<n>
```

`result errors=0` is clean. do not add advice after the summary.

## plan

not written yet. depends on where a dot records its dash ref and how layers merge (see [TODO](../TODO.md)).

## apply

not written yet. the only writer: needs human approval, never automated.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# types.sh [--json] [dash-dir] > README.md: one section per type, from type/*.md, in type/index.md order
set -euo pipefail
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
json=0
[[ ${1:-} == --json ]] && {
  json=1
  shift
}
cd "${1:-$here/../..}"

frontmatter() {
  local fm
  fm="$(awk 'NR==1 && /^---$/ {f=1; next} f && /^---$/ {exit} f' "$1")"
  [[ -n $fm ]] || {
    echo '{}'
    return
  }
  yq -o=json '.' <<<"$fm" 2>/dev/null || yq '.' <<<"$fm"
}

body() {
  awk 'NR==1 && !/^---$/ {b=1} b; /^---$/ && ++c==2 {b=1}' "$1"
}

order() {
  grep -o '](\([a-z-]*\)\.md)' type/index.md | sed 's/^](//; s/\.md)$//'
}

records() {
  local f
  for f in type/*.md type/*/*.md; do
    [[ $(basename "$f") == index.md ]] && continue
    frontmatter "$f" | jq -c --arg file "$f" --arg body "$(body "$f")" '. + {file: $file, body: $body}'
  done
}

# skogai-config

key/value settings, folded across the system, global and local layers. run as `argc config <cmd>` from anywhere under the dash root: `Argcfile.sh` defines `config` and hands it to `bin/skogai-config`.

## layers

each layer is one mise toml file, folded in order, later wins:

1. **system**: `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_SYSTEM_DIR/$SKOGAI_CONFIG_SYSTEM_FILE`
2. **global**: `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_GLOBAL_DIR/$SKOGAI_CONFIG_GLOBAL_FILE`
3. **local**: `$SKOGAI_CONFIG_LOCAL_DIR/$SKOGAI_CONFIG_LOCAL_FILE`

the defaults are the `@env` lines in `bin/skogai-config` (`system/mise.config.toml` and so on), and `mise.config.toml` at the dash root sets the same `_DIR` vars for `mise --env config`. a relative dir is from the dash root: argc cds to the folder holding `Argcfile.sh`, and `ARGC_PWD` is the caller's dir.

keys live under `_.` (mise's free-form namespace), e.g. `_.skogai.config.system.dir`.

## mise does the work

don't rebuild what mise already does:

- read one key from one layer: `mise config get --file <layer> <key>`. a missing key exits `1`.
- write one key: `mise config set --file <layer> <key> <value>`.
- resolved env with the file each value came from: `mise env --env config --json-extended`.
- unset in mise is set via 'foo=false'.
- when the files are in real use/not in sandbox mode the layers are simple flags and the <module> is simply --env=<module>.
  - example1: 
  ```bash 
  mise config --env exampleenv get --system
  [fizz]
  buzz = "bazz"

  [fizz.exampleenv.system]
  path = "/etc/mise/config.exampleenv.toml"

  cat /etc/mise/config.exampleenv.toml 
  [fizz]
  buzz = "bazz"
  exampleenv.system.path = "/etc/mise/config.exampleenv.toml"
  ```

<overview>
The v1 SkogAI routing document contract: YAML frontmatter plus one `<routes>`
XML block. This is the source of truth for document shape; `SKILL.md` keeps the
operating steps.
</overview>

<loading_model>
SKOGAI.md is not natively loaded by Claude Code. It is pulled into context the
same way any other file is: via a native `@`-link written inside a file Claude
Code does auto-load. In practice, a repo's `CLAUDE.md` is itself a router
document:

```markdown
---
permalink: skogai-routing/claude
type: router
---

<routes>

- @SKOGAI.md

</routes>
```

That `<routes>` block is the loading surface. This skill does not implement
loading; it defines what a router document looks like and how to
scaffold/validate one.
</loading_model>

<v1_shape>
A routing file has two parts: YAML frontmatter, then one XML block.

```markdown
---
permalink: skogai-routing/skogai
type: router
---

<routes>

- @MY/PATH/TO/DIR/ - list a directory and allow reading from the files within
- @SUBFOLDER/SKOGAI.md - link to another subfolder's router

</routes>
```

Frontmatter fields:

- `type` (required): always `router` for a routing file. The validator uses it
  to choose the schema/rules for the document body.
- `permalink` (recommended): a stable slug identifying this document,
  independent of its current file path.

<permalink_resolution>
A permalink is `reponame/filename` — a logical identifier, not a filesystem
path. `reponame` names a logical repo, project, or concept, not necessarily
the repo you're currently sitting in. The same `reponame/filename` value
resolves to whichever of these actually exists on the machine:

- `$HOME/reponame/filename.md` (repo checked out directly)
- `$HOME/.local/src/reponame/filename.md` (repo checked out under the shared
  src root)
- `./projects/reponame/filename.md` inside a monorepo (the `projects/<name>/`
  directory is treated as if it were its own future repo)

Example: this repo's own `SKOGAI.md` has permalink `skogai-routing/skogai`. If
`skogai-routing` is vendored as `./projects/skogai-routing/` inside another
repo, the file lives at `./projects/skogai-routing/SKOGAI.md` but the
permalink stays `skogai-routing/skogai` — not `parent-repo/projects/...`. The
permalink must stay stable across all three locations, including if the repo
is later moved between them (e.g. extracted from a monorepo into its own
`$HOME/skogai-routing` checkout).
</permalink_resolution>

`<routes>` body:

- A flat list, one entry per line: `- <path-or-@link> [- <description>]`.
- Blank lines are allowed, but every nonblank line must be a nonempty list
  entry.
- The opening and closing tags each occupy their own line.
- The opening tag has no attributes.
- No second XML block is allowed.
- Markdown prose and fenced examples may appear before or after the routes
  block.
- Entries may be `@`-links or plain paths; both are valid. `@`-links also
  trigger Claude Code auto-inclusion.
- Nothing in `<routes>` is auto-resolved beyond native `@`-linking. A plain
  path is a hint for Claude to read that file when relevant, not an automatic
  injection.

See `../examples/SKOGAI.md.example` for a router with directory/subfolder
routes and `../examples/CLAUDE.md.example` for a minimal router that points at
`@SKOGAI.md`.
</v1_shape>

<future_types>
`<routes>` is the only implemented type in v1. The intended family is typed
documents where a frontmatter `type` matches an XML root tag, such as `router`
with `<routes>`.

Do not invent additional types speculatively. `schemas/router.schema.json` is
deliberately scoped to `router`; extend it, or add sibling schemas, only when a
concrete second type is requested.
</future_types>

type: reference

<overview>
rules for authoring claude.md files as routing files in a hierarchical link chain. complements at-linking.md (which covers @-link mechanics) with the philosophy of when and why to use @ vs plain paths.
</overview>

<rule_1_routers_not_content>
**claude.md files are routers, not content.**

a claude.md routes agents to the right files. it should be lightweight (under ~30 lines). if you're writing paragraphs of content in a claude.md, that content belongs in a separate file that the claude.md routes to.

good: brief identity block + list of paths with descriptions
bad: full documentation, long explanations, inline content
</rule_1_routers_not_content>

<rule_2_at_link_vs_plain_path>
**@-link vs plain path — the loading decision.**

- `@path` = **eagerly loaded** into context. the file contents are injected when the claude.md is read.
- `path` (no @) = **listed for discovery**, loaded on demand when explicitly read.

use @-link for:

- lightweight sub-routers (another claude.md that is itself small)
- small index files (e.g., a table of era names)
- content that IS the point of entering that directory

use plain path for:

- content-heavy files (profiles, full documents, large references)
- files that would bloat context if auto-loaded
- claude.md files that are content-loaders (see rule 4)
  </rule_2_at_link_vs_plain_path>

<rule_3_link_chain_pattern>
**the link chain — each level routes deeper.**

claude.md files form a hierarchy. each level routes to the next, not to everything:

```
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md          (global entry point)
  -> ~/claude/CLAUDE.md      (workspace router)
  -> personal/CLAUDE.md      (area router)
  -> soul/CLAUDE.md          (content loader)
  -> core/CLAUDE.md          (content loader)
```

no level should try to be comprehensive. route to the next level and let it handle the rest. this is progressive disclosure applied to the filesystem.
</rule_3_link_chain_pattern>

<rule_4_router_vs_content_loader>
**router vs content-loader — the critical distinction.**

two types of claude.md:

**routing claude.md** (e.g., `personal/CLAUDE.md`):

- routes to sub-areas
- should NOT @-link content-heavy loaders
- lists content-loaders as plain paths instead

**content-loader claude.md** (e.g., `soul/CLAUDE.md`):

- leaf node that @-links all its content files
- loading content is its explicit job
- when an agent reads this file, they want ALL the content

**the transitive bloat rule:** if a claude.md @-links another claude.md that itself @-links many files, ALL those files load transitively. a router that @-links a content-loader defeats progressive disclosure.

```
# BAD — personal/CLAUDE.md @-links soul/CLAUDE.md which @-links 10 files
# result: entering personal/ loads ALL soul content automatically

# GOOD — personal/CLAUDE.md lists soul/CLAUDE.md as plain path
# result: agent sees soul/ exists, reads it only when needed
```

</rule_4_router_vs_content_loader>

<rule_5_when_to_at_link>
**when to @-link from a router.**

@-link from a routing claude.md ONLY when the target is:

- another lightweight router/index (small claude.md, just a table or short list)
- a small identity or context block that defines "what is this directory"

do NOT @-link:

- content-loader claude.md files (they pull in everything underneath)
- large content files (profiles, documents, full references)
- files where the description in the router is sufficient for discovery
  </rule_5_when_to_at_link>

<rule_6_discoverability_section>
**list non-@-linked files for discoverability.**

files that aren't @-linked should still be listed as plain paths so agents know they exist. use a section like "contents" or "also here":

```markdown
## routes

- @sub-area/CLAUDE.md -- lightweight sub-router

## contents

- profile.md -- agent profile (read when needed)
- journal/ -- session records, append-only
- INDEX.md -- curated highlights index
```

the descriptions matter — they help agents decide whether to read the file without loading it.
</rule_6_discoverability_section>

<rule_7_minimal_default>
**the 99% case: one @-link is enough.**

most claude.md files don't need a routing table at all. if the repo already has a canonical entrypoint (a root `skogai.md`, `SKILL.md`, or equivalent), claude.md's entire job can be:

```markdown
## Routes

- @skogai.md -- canonical entrypoint
```

only add more (a fuller `## Routes` table, additional listed paths) when there's a concrete second route claude needs that the canonical entrypoint doesn't already surface. don't pre-build a table for routes that don't exist yet.
</rule_7_minimal_default>

<companion_reference>
for @-link mechanics (how @ works, permissions, subagent rules, caching behavior), see [at-linking.md](./at-linking.md).
</companion_reference>

# skogai-runner

A Bash command runner built on [argc](https://github.com/sigoden/argc). Register an argc script once, then run it as `argc <name> ...`, with its own help, argument parsing, and completion.

The current implementation is [src/core/main.sh](src/core/main.sh). It generates a main `Argcfile.sh` from a directory of registered scripts. The module work in [best-version-so-far/](best-version-so-far/HANDOVER.md) remains active. We are establishing the basic contracts first, then building out that design. The current Arch package installs the registry runner template.

## Try it from the checkout

Install the tools listed in [mise.toml](mise.toml), then use a temporary registry and main file:

```bash
mise install
demo_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
export ARGC_COMMANDS="$demo_dir/commands"
export ARGC_MAIN="$demo_dir/Argcfile.sh"
export ARGC_TEMPLATE="$PWD/src/core/main.sh"

argc --argc-run "$ARGC_TEMPLATE" register "$PWD/scripts/memory.sh" memory
argc --argc-run "$ARGC_MAIN" --help
argc --argc-run "$ARGC_MAIN" memory show --slug always-commit
argc --argc-run "$ARGC_MAIN" ls
```

The demo memory script prints an action; it does not implement persistent memory. These overrides keep the generated runner outside your normal home configuration. Use a fresh shell afterward to return to the defaults.

## Install on Arch

```bash
cd packaging/arch
makepkg -si
argc --argc-run /usr/share/skogai/core/main.sh sync
```

The package builds the repository's **committed HEAD**, not uncommitted changes. It installs the template at `/usr/share/skogai/core/main.sh`; the user runs `sync` to generate `~/Argcfile.sh`. Sync replaces the target main file, so use `ARGC_MAIN` if that path already holds recipes you want to keep.

With the generated main in place, register scripts using `argc register <file> <name>`, inspect them with `argc ls`, and remove registrations with `argc unregister <name>`. Run `argc sync` after a template update or after changing a script's top-level description.

argc searches for an Argcfile in the current directory and its parents. A nearer project Argcfile takes precedence over the home runner; use `argc --argc-run ~/Argcfile.sh ...` to select it explicitly.
